pages.body:
![](/img/586b1d466a6a534e)

## The importance

A big part of some clients' tasks will revolve around their email, as they may require you to monitor incoming emails to their mailboxes as well as possibly document, organize, and/or respond to incoming emails from their clients. Clients may require virtual assistants to be proficient in email management. Even though it could appear like a straightforward activity, it can greatly ease their load and be of tremendous assistance to them.

## Overview

![](/img/24a59e8071acf4ba)

Managing emails is a process of monitoring, reading, organizing, and responding to email messages. Emails are incredibly useful tools, as they are often used to transmit records, documents, bills, and other information that would otherwise take a long time to be sent via snail mail. This process also includes organizing emails from urgent to non-urgent. Moreover, it involves coordinating important emails with the intended recipient and responding professionally when needed. However, email management is, in and of itself, a time-consuming task.

Email management involves a systematic approach to maximizing email utilization in order to achieve efficiency in reading emails faster and responding to important emails urgently.

Email providers like Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo, and Hotmail offer to create custom email addresses, known as corporate email addresses, for clients who would like to add their own domain names. For example, let's say a client has a website or works for a company that has a website called "[virtualassistant.com](http://virtualassistant.com)", instead of using "name@gmail.com", the client can create his/her corporate email address as "name@virtualassistant.com."

# How To Dos:

In Legal Support Help (LSH), you may have to manage multiple email mailboxes for different clients, or for one client but for different purposes. Being proactive in assisting our customers with email management is crucial for us as virtual assistants. It would be best if we were familiar with how to use Gmail and Outlook as some of them might use one or the other. The following guide will be helpful if you are unsure of how one of these functions.

## Google Mail (Gmail):

![](/img/c196b89c6d2790da)

### Relevant Emails On Top

A great way to keep your inbox organized is to put the relevant emails at the top, such as the ones that are marked important or starred. Gmail also offers other ways to organize your inbox.

1. Go to Settings
2. Select the Inbox tab
3. Click on the “Inbox Type” dropdown selector

![](/img/53f8f5afc56b40db)

### Inbox Types

- **Default: **It shows the emails in the order that they came in, based on date and time.
- **Important First:** Gmail uses its own prediction algorithm to determine which emails are likely to be important, and places them at the top of the inbox with a yellow marker. Everything else goes below that in chronological order.
- **Unread First: **This setting displays unread emails above recent emails. This is especially useful if you use unread emails similar to a to-do list.
- **Starred First: **The starred messages appear on the top of the inbox, followed by everything else in chronological order.
- **Priority Inbox: **Gmail uses its AI (Artificial Intelligence) algorithm to learn what kind of emails you interact (i.e. read, reply, forward, etc.) with the most, and put them at the top of your inbox. This is a great feature for users who have to deal with huge volumes of emails on a daily basis.

### Create Rules to Filter

You can manage your incoming mail using Gmail’s filters to send email to a label, archive, delete, star, or automatically forward your mail.

1. Open [Gmail](https://mail.google.com/)
2. In the right-hand end of the Search bar, click the down arrow.

![](/img/0788c501256b137a)

3. This will show a context-based form. You can then enter your search criteria. If you wish to check if the search criteria worked correctly, you can see what emails show up by clicking Search.

![](/img/eb8a51ba6a4533d0)

4. Once you are satisfied with the search criteria, you can click “Create filter” at the bottom of the search window
5. Choose what you’d like the filter to do.
6. Click “Create filter”
7. Note that when you create a filter to forward messages, only new messages will be affected. ​Additionally, when someone replies to a message you've filtered, the reply will only be filtered if it meets the same search criteria.
8. Alternatively, you may also use a particular message to create a filter.
9. To do this, check the checkbox next to the email you want to use as a template.
10. Click on the “More” vertical ellipsis menu.
11. Click on “Filter messages like these.”
12. You may customize the filter criteria before finalizing the rule.
13. Click “Create filter”

### Labels

Labels are tags that a user can add to emails they send or receive. A user can add more than one label to an email. Users can also customize Labels to add colors.

1. Select any email you’d like to label.
2. Click the Label icon in the action bar to show the context menu

![](/img/76782ae993e262dd)

Here is another way to do it.

1. Click on “More”.

![](/img/d27d07f01abcbf56)

2. Scroll down until you see “Create New Label” and click it.

![](/img/8e74f19a599a81f6)

3. Then you will see this pop up message in which you can create the name of your folder:

![](/img/16c0c60555cbb81d)

### Nest Label

In Google Mail, Nest Label is a subfolder that goes under your parent folder. This can help in sorting emails from your top-level folders when needed. Just click on the empty box and choose whichever folder you want for faster creation of a sub-folder.

1. Click on “Nest Label Under” and select the parent folder that you want to make the subfolder.

![](/img/e40c60afba3bdc2a)

2. Once created it will show like this.

![](/img/8cc9cc9543060ca3)

### Color the Labels

Putting colors on your labels helps you categorize the importance of your folders*.*
1. Hover your cursor over the label that you want to put color. Then, click the three dots beside the name.

![](/img/aeae4953e330f0de)

2. Click “Label Color” and choose the color you want.

![](/img/3ca8f5f2d71f52ed)

### Transfer Emails to Labels

After you have created the parent folder, you can now easily transfer the emails that you want to sort (see steps below), or if it is a very new email, you can just easily drag it to the folder.

1. Search for the email you want to transfer.

![](/img/be7bcc9051c73fdc)

2. If you want to transfer all the emails, just click on "Select All" (see the yellow highlight).

![](/img/823dab6fbe6b94a5)

3. Hover your cursor over one of the highlighted emails, then right-click. Choose "Move to" and then choose the folder you want:

![](/img/56608098a7a5d555)

### Put A Signature On It

You can put the signature of your choosing on new emails or reply or forward

emails.

1. Go to Settings

![](/img/b234d923d36d3411)

2. Click “See All Settings”

![](/img/5579ac802e40dccd)

3. Look for “Signature” and click on “Create New”.

![](/img/921cf05c33cfa49e)

4. Name your signature and hit create.

![](/img/31f196b1edaf536b)

5. Now you can start creating your signature.

![](/img/7fc0c2155f0bd4b2)

### Out-of-Office Reply or Vacation Responder:

This is the option wherein you can set an automatic reply or notification for future emails. People will receive your message containing what you've written in the vacation auto-reply.

1.Go to "Settings"

![](/img/93f2d91b5f7995fc)

2. Click "See All Settings"

![](/img/9e12a14eabb23ef6)

3. Scroll down until you reach "Vacation Responder".
4. Fill out the empty boxes.
5. Choose the date that you want for the first and/or last day of the email.
6. Then, choose where you want to send the response.

![](/img/cd10e97b026c527c)

### Schedule Send

Schedule Send helps you send the emails at a later time or on the schedule that you want. It may be sent a few minutes after the scheduled time
1. At the top left, click compose.

![](/img/bc5468bd01cae073)

2. Create your email

![](/img/29c35beb55a22daf)

3. Click the drop-down arrow beside Send and hit Schedule Send.

![](/img/f7b80252ad7ee95a)

4. Set up the date and time.

![](/img/3faf5ed12f715fa4)

### Templates

Email templates are one of the nicest features available in the email. It enables us to work more quickly and efficiently. It can cut down on the amount of time we need to spend crafting emails when we have many to send in a single day. Time management is crucial in our field of work, so we must devise techniques to complete our tasks right away.

Before you can create a template in Gmail, you have to make sure that the template is enabled in your settings.
1. At the top right, click Settings.

![](/img/94a3d3638b1058fe)

2. Click “See All Settings”.

![](/img/6564feea34a53dd5)

3. At the top, click "Advanced".

![](/img/b1b5f546e9b5a17e)

4. Look for "Templates," then choose "enable" and hit "save changes."

![](/img/716282e444cb3a96)

5. Now you can start creating your template.

![](/img/720fb1c578dcb068)

6. Find the three dots or "More" and click. Hover over to “Templates.” Then, choose “Save draft as templates”. Next, click “Save as new template.”

![](/img/e844ac80e26ef11c)

7. Finally, enter the name of your template and hit “Save”

![](/img/93f4f2d06769db13)

### Edit a Created Template

1. To change a previously saved template, edit the existing message and click “Templates”. Next, choose “Save draft as template” and click the existing template name.

![](/img/d5ed5c1e1603a378)

2. A pop-up message will appear and just hit on “Save”.

![](/img/29c09de293744847)

### Save the Email as a PDF

Clients may occasionally want to have the email confirmation preserved in their files or folders. You will be able to learn how to save email confirmations by following the procedure below.
1. Go to the email that you want to save. At the top right, click on the three dots.

![](/img/aaa7c4197d3b7c4d)

2. Click “Print”

![](/img/4327abd9ea846514)

3. Make sure to choose “Save as PDF” and hit “Save”. Then, name your file.

![](/img/357a427df0db0872)

### Set Up Desktop Notifications For New Emails

If a user prefers real-time engagement, it is strongly recommended to set up desktop notifications. This way, notifications pop up in the top right of the screen every time a new email arrives.

To enable desktop notifications here’s what you have to do:

1. Head to your settings (the gear icon at the top) in the general settings menu.
2. Scroll to ‘Desktop Notifications’ and click on the radio buttons to enable them.

![](/img/a5d81865d17e3aa1)

3. Note that sometimes desktop notifications can become annoying as well as distracting. To avoid this, a user can turn on desktop notifications for emails only marked as “Important.”

### Utilize Nudges

If a user is managing a huge volume of emails in multiple mailboxes, they can potentially miss an important email on Gmail. The Nudge is a feature on Gmail that brings emails back to the top of your inbox when a reply hasn’t been sent by you or a recipient. It is great if you need constant reminders to send replies or follow-ups to important emails.

Nudges in Gmail can be categorized into two kinds:

- **Suggest emails to reply to **Emails you might have forgotten to respond to will be nudged back to the top of your inbox.
- **Suggest emails to follow up on:** Sent emails you might need to follow up on will be nudged back to the top of your inbox.

A user can turn Nudges on/off under the “General” tab in their settings.

![](/img/47f34e1b552b536b)

# Microsoft Outlook

![](/img/8649503a26731b1a)

### Create Folders

1. Go to your outlook website or outlook application:

![](/img/2fbddece78bf3693)

2. Right-click on “Inbox” and click on “New Folder”. Then, you can name the folder.

![](/img/656774d59a43f428)

### Create a Rule

You may filter essential emails using rules you create in Outlook. If your emails are organized, it will take you less time to find the one you're looking for.

1. Right-click on the message you want to create a rule with.

![](/img/e85101d431f9aa6e)

2. Choose the conditions that suit your needs and click "Ok".

![](/img/aaf45ab9bba2c269)

### Add a Signature

1. Open a new message and look for the signature icon on the top right portion.
2. Hover the cursor over and select Signatures.

![](/img/60146b4684a81a5c)

3. Click "New" and type the name for your signature.

![](/img/8598e739c10c5bd2)

### Color that Email

There are times when you receive hundreds or even thousands of emails, and it can be confusing to sort them out very quickly, especially if you have other things to do other than your emails. Putting color on the messages can help you classify the emails from important to non-important.

1. Click the message that you want to sort.

![](/img/82653fc09fc80f8d)

2. On the Ribbon, click the Category Icon then select “All Categories”

![](/img/fa46ad02558d6170)

3. Select New to create a color category

![](/img/06ee1cce5c4d8165)

4. Put the name on it and pick the color you want it to be. Then, hit "OK"

(You can also set a shortcut key.)

![](/img/e6b0cd1449524fd1)

5. You can also change the color anytime you want by clicking on the category and, on the right side, setting the color.

![](/img/456e7b759eb342d0)

### Save the Email as a PDF

1. Click on “New Mail”, then look for the three dots at the top right corner.

![](/img/cb4aa8293f64a408)

2. Once you see the email, click “Print”.

![](/img/a1c226f8524ad7a8)

3. Make sure to choose “Save as PDF” and hit “Save”. Then, name your file.

![](/img/953fc2a3371172b1)
![](/img/c322fc5128dd4459)

### Templates in Outlook

Creating a template in Outlook does not require any activation. Follow the guide below to help you in creating a template in Outlook.
1. Click on “New Mail”, then look for the three dots on the bottom.

![](/img/f2c2b8d2c2537d9f)

2. Hit on “My Templates”

![](/img/6a782f74df3aa8c3)

3. Scroll down to the bottom and click “Template.”

![](/img/eb108bdd1f4060e9)

4. Write the title of your template and the content of the template. Finally, hit “Save”.

![](/img/3843d0a014772ef2)

# Phishing

![](/img/a8a8dd141cc7ac7c)

## What is phishing?

*Phishing is a deceptive practice that's frequently carried out through the phone and email. It poses as an engaging, reliable, and helpful source or piece of material in an effort to persuade you into disclosing personal, private, and sensitive information.*

### What is a phishing email?

*** It tricks you into replying to emails that seem like they came from a friend or coworker and clicking links that pretend to be emailed from such people. Some phishing attempts could appear to be from a trustworthy business or website.*

### How to detect phishing emails:

*In our line of work, phishing emails are common, so it's critical to be able to recognize a legitimate email from a suspicious one. Devastating unintentional information disclosure around the world are still rampant due to these phishing attacks.*

*If one is able to identify a phishing email immediately, it can prevent a disastrous data breach. Here are the samples of phishing emails.*

***1. Google Docs Scam - One of the well-known phishing methods poses as the Google Docs Scam. It will seem as though the sender is someone you know. You will receive an email invite to click on its link to view a document, which then directs you to a page that looks almost exactly like the Gmail login page. The moment you accept the invitation to allow access to a chosen account, the attacker has full control of your Google account.*

**

![](/img/7027db0900bd7277)

***2. Dropbox scam- Dropbox features are somewhat similar to Google Docs'. This kind of phishing is also very pervasive. The Dropbox phishing email often operates by warning the recipient that the attached "file" is too large to open directly and requires a quick "click on this link." This page is frequently found inside Dropbox itself, eagerly waiting to collect your information.*

![](/img/e0af73d38be8e61b)

![](/img/f7f1e056ed3636f8)

***3. Email from friends, families, coworkers, or colleagues ***- A malicious attachment or link is frequently included in an email from someone you may believe to be familiar with and, when clicked, will install harmful software into your computer or device. So before clicking that link, make sure to contact the sender to verify the email.

***4. Unusual Activity Notification Scam ***- An odd activity scam might have many different sources, and this is only one of them. An attacker can utilize any app, website, or platform to carry out this harmful method, whether it originates from a trustworthy website or even your Instagram account.

![](/img/021b02f25fbd6611)

***5. Email Account Upgrade Scam ***- Scammers may pose as reputable email providers like Microsoft and Google or even your company's IT department in order to trick you into upgrading your email account. Sometimes emails may not have obvious grammatical problems or complex requests, and the link itself would appear to direct to a safe "https" web page. When prompted for personal information,*it's a good idea to hover your mouse over the link itself, as the text itself often doesn’t represent the true destination of the link.**
***

![](/img/cbe4f6e8d2efe2f3)

![](/img/8f6273349e40c53b)

***6. Fake Invoice Scam*** - This con exploits a user's sense of urgency and panic to persuade them to pay for products or services they have never even requested or received.

![](/img/55543c2a5a7b0af3)

**7. Bank Scam **- These emails frequently have the bank's logo and some plausible small print at the bottom. This scam seeks to put its victims into a panicked state by sending them messages like, "There's an issue with your account, please click here to fix it." They also have fine print that appears to be authentic, so beware.

![](/img/1c605cce3cec2015)

![](/img/c6ed9fcec88796ec)

pages.title: Getting Started with Zapier
pages.summary: Zapier is a tool that allows you to connect your favorite web apps to each other and move information between them automatically.
pages.body:
## What is Zapier?

Zapier is a tool that allows you to connect your favorite web apps to each other and move information between them automatically.

This allows you to forget mundane tasks and let you focus on what really matters.

![44v4ntALkPnNT2SbhY7SDJtledkpFKKfx2EDJaXDCsAcMZH2qAnGjS97Cl-0KUGxdtbUrD5kMA-DuxCYn5fDP7RrsYyNmR-juTO5L62zBjRnlXIJyjF-nGi5CvuUQ6mP6txIljQJV2U](/img/3a23542db6683796)

## Make life easier using Zapier

- Engage your leads instantly.
- Automatically import new customers.
- Notify your team about new opportunities.
- Consolidate information in a spreadsheet.
- Save time.

## Terminology

- **App : **The web service or application you want to connect with Zapier.
- **Zap : **Zap is our term for the automated workflows you set up between your apps.
- **Trigger : **A Trigger is the event that starts you Zap.
- **Action : **An Action is an event a Zap performs after it is triggered.
- **Tasks : **The actions your Zaps perform for you. A single Zap can perform more than one task.
- **Task History : **The place in your account where you can see all the actions your Zaps have performed for you.

## Unleashing your Zaps

Zapier allows you to connect the software (currently 2,000+ apps) you use every day and automate your workflows without having to use any code.

All you have to do is pick an event (trigger) that sets Zapier in motion, then choose what work should happen automatically.

![95MLLeRybUqKnWCuhJ6VZm0Kj32KNoAUGQpIplmMBCcyjch-tQ2KX9EEzgKCBu_jQ8n1Xm497ePJm_78cu0MZzDH2ubC1HrRXb2ZXuMzhONY3ZC4klGFoGb1zCWdXJ7C8FTqNmf43ew](/img/62eb8d412ddaa947)

### *For the example above, whenever a form is filled up (new entry), it will add automatically to Google Spreadsheet as a lead.*

### Here's another example:

![PNBNpjwfn9pIUwIhbc-IeQ6dR9NZAu8A76x_rDsA67jgFux4Zeng6dF0lGgV-zJIFB9DELOgjr-o8empqmVnV9odkvcwrr1evSUpWOcNbSWEe2peqkba_Wl5EqI03bLtdLVkhRaq3Bo](/img/33d1b04eab027c50)

### *For the example above, whenever there is a new lead from Facebook it will send an email or follow up via email automatically.*

### Here’s a sample for a multi step flow:

![N_ScADwVP108_fWX1BZsVma284CC5Pu9dYw4vUcvC3yT3cwhNeeIE6LSxDlE1JiDji05tOFauIAjMtIJkHkGDNgBEdqlomLY2h7CiD9peDmgHOenzK-Qh_cSu5DB77tiYUnrdAI5Css](/img/ce45dc91c625eb0c)

### *For the example above, when someone fills up your Facebook lead form:*

1. It will send an email automatically to reply via email.
2. Alert your team automatically in slack so it will be easy to follow up.

You can create one zap to do several jobs for you and the possibilities are endless. There are zaps that can save your organization time across the board.

## How to Create a Zap that will add info from Google Forms in Google Sheet

1. Select Create a Zap.
2. Select Google Forms as your First app.
3. Choose an Event or Trigger.
4. Connect your Google account.
5. Select the Form.
6. List of fields from your Google Forms will show up when you click Test Trigger
7. Select Google Sheet as your Second app.
8. Choose an Event or trigger.
9. Connect your Google account.
10. Select the sheet to use.
11. All columns in your sheet will show up as separate fields.
12. You can map the fields from Google Forms to columns used in Google Sheet.

![HjVMgo-Uy8kfi8idNsCExtK8V7kp3HgnSrYqNRGb9fMRkz24MKqO8IRE7546MvifdNCsAYff9QL1ORs62hsy5btQ4JhScfTUyQWBFI97KJH6sRrc-TNCW7buUrVwF_ri3hbfm9HiWUg](/img/5982b15a40e27b1a)

## How to Create a Zap using Google Calendar to remind you in Slack, 30 minutes before a Zoom meeting starts

1. Select Google Calendar as your First app.
2. Choose Event Start as your trigger.
3. Connect your Google account.
4. Input 30 in Time Before and select Minutes in Time Before (Unit).
5. Select Filter as your Second app.
6. Filter data from Google Calendar to contain only Zoom.
7. Select Delay by Zapier as your Third app.
8. Under Customize Event input the Start of Event and subtract by 3.
9. Select Slack as your Fourth app.
10. Select Slack and Send Direct Message.
11. Under Customize Channel Message input your Slack ID.
12. Input the Google Calendar data in Message text as desired.

pages.title: LSH Legal Jargon
pages.summary: File is a legal process where the written complaint or petition which is the opening step in a lawsuit and subsequent documents, including an answer, demurrer, motions, petitions and orders are submitted to the clerk …
pages.body:
## FILE vs SERVE

**File **is a legal process where the written complaint or petition which is the opening step in a lawsuit and subsequent documents, including an answer, demurrer, motions, petitions and orders are submitted to the clerk of Court. While **Serve** is the delivery of legal document such as copy of written complaint and summons to the defendant to informed of a lawsuit against him.

## Parties to the Case

**Plaintiff** the party who initiates a lawsuit or action in a civil case and complainant in a criminal prosecution.

**Defendant** is the party sued in a lawsuit or the party charged with a crime in a criminal prosecution.

## Person

Can either be a natural person (individual) or artificial person (legal entity such as corporations or a government instrumentality).

## Case Details/Information

### Court Information (Venue and/or Jurisdiction)

**Venue **is the Court where a lawsuit may or should be tried. In U.S, every state has rules in determining the proper venue for different types of lawsuit. Criminal cases will be prosecuted in the state or district where the alleged crime was committed.

*Eg. Nevada: Clark County, District Court; Florida: County Court of the 9th Judicial Circuit, Orange County, Florida*

**Jurisdiction** - power/authority of the court. It is the limit of a judicial authority or the extent to which a court of law can exercise its authority over suits, cases, appeals, etc.; Hierarchy of Courts.

*Eg. Nevada: Justice Court, District Court, Supreme Court; Florida: Trial Court (Circuit or County), District Courts of Appeal, Supreme Court*

pages.title: Going beyond Zapier Basics
pages.summary: Schedule is a Zapier app that can be used for recurring tasks. Schedule lets you determine when a Zap should trigger (every day, every week, every month, or even every hour).
pages.body:
## Schedule by Zapier

Schedule is a Zapier app that can be used for recurring tasks. Schedule lets you determine when a Zap should trigger (every day, every week, every month, or even every hour).

![](/img/ba188fd9c22f32fb)

## Email Parser by Zapier

Email Parser lets you extract information from your emails.

1. Set up a parser mailbox at parser.zapier.com

![](/img/9883632da1cc8fba)

2. Forward emails to your unique Zapier email address
3. Create a template to determine which information is pulled from the email

![](/img/c51e1c4989204f3f)

## Filter by Zapier

Add conditional logic to your Zaps with a filter step. This will let you check information arriving in your trigger step and only continue to subsequent steps in the Zap if that condition has been met.

![](/img/4a2c26f63fe9eb1c)

**Condition filters**

- (text) Exactly matches
- (text) Does not exactly match
- (text) Contains
- (text) Does not contain
- (text) Is in
- (text) Is not in
- (text) Start with
- (text) Does not start with
- (text) Ends with
- (number) Does not end with
- (number) Greater than
- (number) Less than
- (date/time) After
- (date/time) Before
- (date/time) Equals
- (boolean) Is true
- (boolean) Is false
- Exist
- Does not exist

## Paths by Zapier

Smarter workflows that think for you. Zapier’s new logic tool lets you build multiple outcomes into one Zap, so you can automate anything you imagine.

No need to duplicate your Zaps or write any code. You can use Paths to build in options to make work easier with automation

1. Add your Paths - Use paths to reroute data from one app to multiple scenarios. After you setup your trigger app. Select “Paths”
2. Set Conditions - For each path, you can set the rules for what’s allowed to pass through. Add as many rules as you want.
3. Add more Paths - Add more paths to create more routes. Each paths lead to different outcome, making your Zap more powerful

![](/img/eac93d38f2307fd3)

## Delay by Zapier

Put your Actions on hold for a specified amount of time before sending data to another app or continuing to additional action steps. You can set up scheduled emails, get notified of incomplete tasks, send automatic follow-ups , and automate other tasks on your timeline.

![](/img/d15c7dfcf5ca0613)

## What is Zap Sharing?

**Zap sharing is a simple way to share a copy of your favorite automated workflow with colleagues, clients, or your friends and followers.**

![](/img/8bc643e530359c8e)

![](/img/c321edf9ae4edf14)

pages.title: Introduction to Zapier Formatter: Text, dates, time
pages.summary: Formatter is a built in Zapier tool that allows you to take information (also called data ) from one app and transform it into a different format before passing it on to another app.
pages.body:
## Formatter by Zapier

**Formatter is a built-in Zapier tool that allows you to take information (also called *data*) from one app and transform it into a different format before passing it on to another app.**

## What can a formatter do?

- Text : Over 20 options for editing text, including capitalize, truncate, split, replace, and extract email addresses or phone numbers.
- Date/times: Change dates into the format you need and subtract or add time.
- Numbers: Format numbers, currencies, or phone numbers and perform math operations.
- Utilities: Look up values, create line items, or return a value from a list ased on the data received.

![](/img/fed793599bfe1d09)

## Remove HTML tags

When to use it: If you need to turn text formatted with HTML tags into plain text.

What it does: Removes HTML tags so that formatted text shows up as plain text.

![](/img/c082b88822739e76)

## Replace

When to use it: If you need to replace any character, word, or phrase in your trigger step information with another word or phrase.

What it does: Replaces text in the new text you specify

![](/img/58b7be22456c69f6)

## Truncate

When to use it: If you need to shorten text from your trigger step.

What it does: Limits your text to a specific character length and deletes anything over that.

![](/img/b216c2ae9e5e9733)

## Split text

When to use it: If you need to break up text from your trigger step.

What it does: Splits your content at a specified separator (e.g., a space or a comma) or at line breaks

![](/img/4f3479f3ade1c7f1)

## Default value

When to use it: If your action step requires information that’s missing from your trigger step.

What it does: Checks the field in your trigger step and adds default text if it’s empty.

![](/img/1818fea64e583bea)

## Format date/time

When to use it: When your action step requires a date or time in a specific format, such as mm/dd/yyyy.

What it does: Changes the format of a date or time.

![](/img/cfb3dfcea72b6a07)

## Add/subtract time

When to use it: If you need to change a date or time

What it does: adds or subtracts minutes, hours, days, or months from a date or time value before using it in your action step

![](/img/552f4d759c241800)

pages.title: United States Time Zones
pages.summary: The United States uses four standard time zones. From east to west they are Eastern Standard Time (EST), Central Standard Time (CST), Mountain Standard Time (MST), and Pacific Standard Time (PST)
pages.body:
## Introduction

The United States uses four standard time zones. From east to west they are **Eastern Standard Time (EST), Central Standard Time (CST), Mountain Standard Time (MST), and Pacific Standard Time (PST)**

![](/img/6efb3b5dc9aed7d3)

- **Daylight Saving Time** begins at **2:00 a.m. local** time on the **second Sunday in March**.
- On the **first Sunday in November** areas on Daylight Saving Time **return to Standard Time at 2:00a.m.**

*The names in each time zone change along with Daylight Saving Time. Eastern Standard Time (EST) becomes Eastern Daylight Time (EDT), and so forth. Arizona, Puerto Rico, Hawaii, U.S. Virgin Islands and American Samoa do not observe Daylight Saving Time.*

## United States Timezone Map

![](/img/bd79fd51c9ae1213)

## Time Zones States & Area Codes

United St

### Pacific Time Zone States

Pacific time zone is also referred to as PST for **Pacific Standard Time and PDT for Pacific Daylight Time**. The pacific time zone. During PST has an offset of -5 hours.

- California
- Nevada
- Oregon
- Washington

### Mountain Time Zone States

Mountain time zone is also referred to as MST for **Mountain Standard Time and PDT for
Mountain Daylight Time**. The pacific time zone.

- Arizona
- Colorado
- Idaho
- Montana
- New Mexico
- Utah
- Wyoming

### Central Time Zone States

Central time zone is also referred to as CST for Central Standard Time and CDT for **Central
Daylight Time**. The central time zone.

- Araknsans
- Illinois
- Iowa
- Kansas
- Louisiana
- Minnesota
- Mississippi
- Missouri
- Oklahoma
- North Dakota
- South Dakota
- Texas
- Wisconsin

### Eastern time Zone States

Eastern time zone is also referred to as EST for **Eastern Standard Time and EDT for Eastern Daylight
Time.** The eastern time zone. **During EST has an offset of -5 hours**. During** EDT or daylight savings, the
eastern time zone has an offset of -4 hours for UTC-GMT**. States in the eastern time zone include Main,
Vermont, New York, New Jersey, and Ohio. Some states like Alabama belong to Eastern and Central
time zones.

- Connecticut
- Delaware
- Georgia
- Maine
- Maryland
- Massachusetts
- New Hampshire
- New Jersey
- New york
- North Carolina
- Ohio
- Pennsylvania
- Rhode Island
- South Carolina
- Vermont
- Virgina
- West Verginia

* States with both Eastern and Central Zones:*

- Alabama
- Florida
- Indiana
- Kentucky
- Michigan
- Wisconsin
- Tennessee

### Area Codes: [Look Up by State and City](https://www.allareacodes.com/)

## US Time Zone Chart

pages.title: CMS - Lawmatics
pages.summary: The pipeline is a great tool to keep track of the progress of your matters in Lawmatics. You can have a pipeline for any of your firm’s processes, including intake, case management, or a flow specific to a certain pra…
pages.body:
## I. GETTING STARTED

### A. PIPELINE OVERVIEW

The pipeline is a great tool to keep track of the progress of your matters in Lawmatics. You can have a pipeline for any of your firm’s processes, including intake, case management, or a flow specific to a certain practice area. The pipeline gives you an at-a-glance view of the steps in this process, and where your matters fall on those steps.

To create a pipeline you’ll go to the settings gear in the top right of any Lawmatics page, and then select Pipeline Settings on the left. This is where you can build and edit any of your pipelines.

When you create a new pipeline, you will give the pipeline a name, and you have the option to enter a description.

![](/img/6b8a5f5b976f8000)

You will also need to select which matter status(es) you want to be shown on the pipeline. This will decide what status of matters will automatically be displayed when you view the pipeline. If you are building one to be used for intake, you will want to use PNC as the status. If you are building a pipeline for case management, use hired. You could also make one catch-all pipeline and set it to show multiple statuses.

Lastly, you will also see the toggle for “Intake Pipeline?”. Selecting yes will show the total value of matters in each pipeline stage as well an expected value prediction.

![](/img/2e1201ee410e1378)

Once you have created the pipeline itself, you will then add the stages for that pipeline. Keep in mind when creating your pipeline stages that you can trigger automations when a matter enters a certain stage, or you can also move a matter to a given stage via automation. You can also move matters between pipelines via automation.

To give an example of when you would assign a pipeline stage automatically, you may have a stage for “Consult Scheduled”. You can use an automation to move a matter into this stage immediately when a consultation is booked.

You’ll want to be precise with your stage names to avoid any confusion that could be caused by ambiguous stage names. If your stage is called “Initial Consultation”, you will be left wondering “has this matter scheduled their consultation?” or “has the consultation already happened?”.

After you have finished adding in your stages, you can view your pipeline by going to CRM -> Pipeline.

![](/img/5e038f42abad5da2)

In the top left, you will see the name of the pipeline. Once you have created more than one pipeline, you can switch between pipelines by clicking the small arrow next to the word Intake above.

On the right, you’ll notice that you have the option to show the “No Stage” column. This column will contain matters that don’t have any stage assigned yet.

You also have the option to “Show All Matters”. Selecting this button will override the Status(es) that you have chosen for this pipeline and show all matters at their respective stages, regardless of status.

If you want to manually move a matter from one pipeline to another, you can do so from that matter’s profile page. Under the matter’s name, you will see a box showing what stage they are currently in. When you click on this drop down you’ll see all of your pipelines and stages, and you can select whichever stage you want to move the matter to.

![](/img/aadd4291c743c495)

### B. GENERAL SETTINGS OVERVIEW

There are various settings and customizations in Lawmatics that you’ll want to be familiar with while getting. You’ll find these by clicking the **gear icon** near the top right corner of your screen. You will see all the various settings listed on the left sidebar.

First, make sure you’ve set up all of your user settings, starting with My Settings, and advise other users at your firm to do the same. [Click here](https://help.lawmatics.com/article/206-settings-setup) for a helpful video on getting started with these settings.

Once you’ve done that, you’ll move onto the firm-wide settings. These settings only need to be done once for the firm, and then they’ll be set for all additional users. Keep in mind that settings can always be edited if needed down the road, nothing is set in stone.

**Firm Settings**

Here you can upload the firm’s logo, you’ll ideally want to choose one that is square or circular, since it will fit in the circle better than a rectangular logo.

Next, you’ll enter the firm’s email address, as well as phone number and address. This email address will be referred to as the **Firm Email** in Lawmatics, and it will be an option to select as the ‘send from’ any time you’re sending emails out of Lawmatics. If you have a general info/admin email address, we suggest using that here. If not, you can just use your regular email address.

As you scroll down you can enter additional addresses if your firm has multiple. You’ll want to select those addresses in the Locations section, and add in any other location options like Phone Call or Virtual Meeting, etc. These Locations will be used for setting the location of your appointments.

Lastly on this page, you’ll see a signature block for the Firm Email. This will be used for the Firm Email referenced above.

**Pipeline Settings**

Learn about creating your pipeline [here](/#/go/952181).

**Practice Areas**

Learn how to create your practice areas [here.](https://help.lawmatics.com/article/213-practice-areas)

**Custom fields**

Learn about custom fields [here](https://help.lawmatics.com/article/168-video-custom-field-overview).

**Matter Settings**

Relationship types are used to link multiple contacts to a matter. Every matter will have just one contact as the primary contact, but if there are additional contacts related to that matter you can connect them via relationships.

Your types could be things like Spouse, Co-Client, Child, Parent, Authorized Contact, etc. Once you’ve created your relationship types on the Matter Settings page, you’ll then be able to use them to link contacts on any matter.

Make types repeatable when there could be multiple contacts in that type for a given matter. So for example, Spouse would not be repeatable, but Sibling would be.

On this page you’ll also see a section for Matter Sub-Statuses. The 3 primary statuses for matters in Lawmatics are as follow:

· **PNC** (Potential new clients, these are your active leads going through your intake)

· **Hired** (These are your clients, PNCs that hired the firm)

· **Lost** (These were once PNCs, but ended up not hiring the firm)

You can create custom sub-statuses that will fall under those 3 main categories. You likely won’t need any sub-statuses for PNCs, since you have the pipeline to manage those.

For Hired, you might want sub-statuses for Open Case vs. Closed Case.

Most importantly, you’ll want to create sub-statuses for your various Lost reasons. This will be useful for your reporting and analytics on lost leads. Some examples include (but are not limited to): Hired other firm, Referred out, Firm rejected, Financial reasons, Unresponsive, etc.

**Contact Settings**

Create custom contact types, such as Referral Partner, Judge, Client’s Family Member, etc.

**Event Settings**

If your firm has multiple types of appointments that clients can book, you can add them as custom event types. You’ll start with the Initial Consultation type built in, but you could also add things like Follow Up Meeting, Discovery Call, Signing Meeting, etc.

We do not suggest creating different types for your different locations, so don’t create “Phone Consultation”, etc. Instead, you’ll use the Location of the appointment to differentiate these.

If you have an external calendar synced, you’ll also create your custom booking links on this page. Check out this article to learn more about that: [https://help.lawmatics.com/article/134-custom-calendar-booking-links](https://help.lawmatics.com/article/134-custom-calendar-booking-links)

**Marketing Settings **

Create a source for each of your various marketing channels. You’ll see that the Referrals source comes built in.

Some examples of sources you may have are Google PPC, Social Media, Radio Ads, Events, Avvo, etc.

When you add in a new source, you’ll have the option to include a UTM_Source. If the source is an online advertisement, that ad/landing page should have a UTM_Source code that you can plug in here. If not, just leave that section blank.

You can also select your spend frequency, so if you want to log your spend on this source per day, week, or month. It doesn’t need to be the same dollar amount each interval, this just determines what those intervals will be.

Once you’ve created a source, you can also add campaigns. For example, if you meet PNCs at events/conferences, that might be the name of your source, and then you can add campaigns for each specific event you go to.

**Tracking Settings**

Enter in your firm’s website to generate a tracking pixel. Click the eyeball icon to view and copy this tracking snippet.

Paste this snippet on the code for your website (this step done outside of Lawmatics) to start tracking leads that come into Lawmatics from your online sources.

If you’ve entered a UTM_Source for your online sources, mentioned in the section above, then this tracking pixel will register that code, and match it to the appropriate source when applicable.

**Integrations**

You can connect your account for any of the other systems listed on this page that your firm uses.

Lawmatics has also an app on Zapier, which you can find here: [https://zapier.com/apps/lawmatics/integrations](https://zapier.com/apps/lawmatics/integrations)

** Manage Users**

Here you can add and remove users from your firm.

You also have the option to create custom roles for your users. This allows you to select different permissions for each role, in case you want to restrict certain users from viewing certain areas of Lawmatics. Click the Manage Roles button to create these.

When you invite a new user, they will receive an email to activate their account and sign into your firm. They’ll then want to customize their User Settings, like their email signature, calendar sync, etc.

**Import**

You can migrate your current contact/database into Lawmatics. This is useful if you want to use Lawmatics to send out newsletters or other mass marketing emails.

Check out this article walking you through the importing process: [Importing](https://help.lawmatics.com/article/133-importing-matters-and-contacts---including-custom-field-imports)

Once you’ve gone through this article and formatted your spreadsheet, we strongly suggest reviewing the spreadsheet with our support team before importing.

### C. USER SETTINGS

**My Settings:**

1. Go to the settings page in Lawmatics

![](/img/08d0f5156109fa9c)

2. This will immediately take you to the "My Setting" page
3. On this page you will verify if your "Personal Information" is correct

![](/img/29a45a70232e120c)

4. Add a picture

![](/img/691824665bf025d2)

- *This picture will be included in Signature Request emails*

5. Add your email signature

![](/img/da0cb1891e18d2b3)

- It is recommend that you turn on the toggle to include your email signature on emails sent from you
- If you do not want your signature to be double spaced, press shift+enter in order to add a line break without skipping a line
- You can use the "General Fields" dropdown to merge your firm information from the "Firm Settings" page
- We do not have an HTML editor for email signatures, so you will want to stick with images and hyperlinks
- When adding an image, check the size of the image before pasting it in the text editor. You will usually not want that image to be more than 3 inches wide.

**Notifications:**

1. Click on Notifications below My Settings

![](/img/756a63a53d4c3ccd)

2. You will see In-App and Email options

![](/img/d0b2448b78179f0c)

- Notifications toggled on for Email will be sent to the email address on your My Setting page
- Notifications toggled on for In-App will go to the exclamation point on the upper right of your screen

![](/img/fe864aec161060b2)

3. The changes to this page will save automatically

**Mail Sync:**

Our mail sync will sync over any emails and attachments that are being sent between you and a matter in you work email to Lawmatics, as long as the matter exists in Lawmatics with the same email address.

1. Click on Mail Sync below Notifications

![](/img/df50ca0e7b493484)

2. Select your email provider, click *I have read the instructions and I'm ready to connect my
account,* click *CONNECT EMAIL ACCOUNT, *enter the email address you would like to connect, and
click *SIGN IN*

![](/img/742721829befb2d6)

3. Toggle on *Sync Email *and *Sync Attachments*

![](/img/96ca3990ef01a4d4)

### C. GETTING STARTED OVERVIEW

[Watch here
](https://help.lawmatics.com/article/170-getting-started-overview)
D. PRACTICE AREAS

**Setting Up Practice Areas**

Practice areas will be used in a few integral ways in your account. They will be used in your automations to make sure that potential clients are getting forms, documents, and email specific to their case. You will also be able to track the number of potential clients entering the CRM by practice area and conversion rates by practice area on our Analytics page.

Please follow the instructions below to add your practice areas:

1. Go to your settings page in Lawmatics

![](/img/a745cb19c1f11951)

2. Select Practice Areas on the left of your screen

![](/img/33e32540c0181d02)

3. Click the Add New Practice Area button at the bottom of the screen

![](/img/ef6c873d24347d46)

4. Select a practice area from the list or Create Custom Practice Area at the top of the list

![](/img/3d5b001f2e59c152)

5. Select a color can click Save

![](/img/617c2b4bd54056a6)

**FAQs:**

**How granular should I be with naming my practice areas? Should I just create one for “Family Law”, or should I have separate ones for “Adoption”, “Divorce”, etc?**

Ask yourself whether or not those matters will have any different procedures, and/or if it will be insightful to your firm to track them separately. Do I want to send a different intake form automatically to my Adoption matters vs. my Divorce matters? Will it be useful to know that I had X number of Adoption matters contact my firm this month, compared to X number of Divorce matters? If the answer to either of those questions is yes, then they should be separate practice areas.

**Certain staff members at my firm only work with specific practice areas, can they filter matters to only see the practice areas that are relevant for them?**

Yes, on the Matters page under the CRM tab you will see a funnel icon on the far right column. Type in the desired practice area, as shown below, then click the plus sign on the right to save that filtered view.

![](/img/cde7dc8e1916f1d5)
![](/img/1af711b86759ba01)

![](/img/168f11842d068f3e)

**Can I filter the pipeline based on practice area?**

Yes, first hover on CRM and select Pipeline. Then click the funnel on the right side of the screen.

![](/img/4624657099f121ca)

Select your filter based on the desired practice area, and give that filter a name. Then click Save View.

![](/img/b6bee2a373d4bf8e)

You can now select this view from the drop down menu, shown below.

![](/img/9ae10bc9fc7f39eb)

## II. BILLING

**Invoice Types**
In order to send invoices and receive payment via automations you will need to have invoice types set up. In order to create invoice types, simply navigate to the Settings page and select Firm Settings form the left side navigation panel. You will see a section about midway down the screen entitled 'Invoice Types', as depicted below.

![](/img/8ba16ddfec6e30a4)

You should create an invoice type for all the different line items that you charge for. For example, 'Retainer Fee', 'Flat Fee' and 'Consultation Fee' are all great examples of items that should be created as individual invoice types.

***IMPORTANT - When an invoice type is created, a corresponding field will be created on matters designed to capture the amount of the invoice for the particular matter. We automatically create the custom field for you and we add the word 'Amount' to the end of the invoice type name when creating the field. Be sure not to add the word 'Amount' yourself to the invoice type name.*

**Default value**

When creating an invoice type, you have the option to set a default value for the invoice type. This will create a default value that gets filled in as the amount in the invoice type's custom field. You can always change the value of this field.

Once you have invoice types setup, you will be able to send invoices via automations and also use the payment of an invoice type as a trigger for an automation. You can also always send a one off invoice manually from the matter details page by clicking on Send Invoice from the bottom action bar.

## III. CLIENT PORTAL OVERVIEW

### A. GIVING CLIENTS ACCESS TO CLIENT PORTAL

Access to the client portal is given on a contact by contact basis. This means that if you have several relationships attached to a matter you give each one of them their own access to login to their own portal. You also grant access on a matter by matter basis, so if you have a client with two matters, giving them portal access to one will not automatically give them portal access to their other matter.

Signature documents, file requests and appointments scheduled the relate to a matter will be automatically shared with a contact in their portal if they are a party to the item being shared.

***To grant portal access to a contact:***

1. Navigate to the matter details page for the matter you want to give access to.
2. Click on the share icon to the right of the case title.

![](/img/60265af538502d17)

3. Here you will see a list of all the contacts associated with this matter that can be granted portal access.
Simply check the ***"Has Access?"*** box on the contacts you want to give access to and then click ***Save***.

![](/img/e81e685aeeb86761)

4. If you need to ever revoke portal access, simply uncheck that same field for the contact you want to revoke
access for and click ***Save***.

### B. SHARING APPOINTMENTS WITH CLIENT PORTAL

*Currently, all appointments created on a matter will be shared with all contacts associated with that matter in their client portal.*

### C. SHARING A DOCUMENT WITH A CLIENT'S PORTAL

1. Access the Files tab from the matter details page.
2. Find the document you want to share and click the share icon on the right side of the document in the list.

![](/img/f3513c47210482a1)

3. Here, you will see a list of all contacts with portal access for this matter. Simply check the contacts you
would like to share this document with and then click ***"Share"***.

### D. SHARING A TASK WITH CLIENT'S PORTAL

Task sharing with the client portal in Lawmatics makes it easy to assign tasks to clients. Use this feature if there are tasks that you need your clients to complete. The task will appear in their portal and they will even be able to mark it as done when they've completed it.

1. Create a task
2. From the task creation window, you will see an option that says ***"ASSIGN TASK TO CONTACTS"***. Click that header to reveal all the contacts with portal access on that particular matter. Select the contacts you would like to assign this task to and click ***Create Task*** when ready.

![](/img/98144768b17698be)

### E. HOW TO MANAGE YOUR SUBDOMAIN

The client portal is the first feature in Lawmatics to utilize custom subdomains. This means that clients will be able to access your portal by visiting a more customized URL. If your law firm name is Spiegel Law Group, you could have the url ***spiegellawgroup.portal.lawmatics.com***. We will default the subdomain to contain the name of your firm as it is in Lawmatics, however, you can change this.

***In order to change your subdomain:***

1. Navigate to the Settings page
2. Click on Firm Settings from left side of screen
3. Click on Gear Icon on top right of Firm Settings data

![](/img/b06854962d53a1ad)

4. Towards the very bottom of the list of Firm Settings fields you will see a field called "Subdomain". Enter in
any word(s) into that field. Please note that you can only use letters or digits and there must be no white
space.

5. Click save when ready and whatever is entered into that field will be your new domain. The format will
always be [YOURCUSTOMDOMAIN].portal.lawmatics.com

## IV. CALENDAR

### A. SYNCING YOUR CALENDAR

You’ll start by going to Settings -> Calendar Settings. This is a user setting, meaning that each user in your firm can customize their own calendar settings.

Click Connect Calendar, and then select your calendar provider from the list provided. We can sync with any of the following options:

![](/img/db9fbdc3277c57cf)

If you are syncing an Office 365 calendar, you will also need to make sure that you have admin privileges. If you don’t, you’ll need to share this link with the appropriate person at your firm who is the admin on the account: [https://app.cronofy.com/oauth/authorize/admin/office365?client_id=D_SMNVnpY_xdAXzJ3Q-7j8L1Th5ImpBD](https://app.cronofy.com/oauth/authorize/admin/office365?client_id=D_SMNVnpY_xdAXzJ3Q-7j8L1Th5ImpBD)

If you are syncing an iCloud calendar, you will need to generate an app specific password. Follow the instructions found [here](https://www.imore.com/how-generate-app-specific-passwords-iphone-ipad-mac) to do so.

Once you have selected your provider you will be prompted to agree to the terms of service and sign in to your account for that calendar. This will not be your Lawmatics login credentials, but rather your credentials for the calendar provider.

Once your calendar has been synced, you should see a screen similar to the one below:

![](/img/dae97ef07f6a1049)

If you have more than one calendar being used on your external provider (for example, you might have work, personal, holidays, birthdays, etc) you can select which of these you want to be used to sync events, and which should be used to pull availability.

You might only have the one calendar, as you see in the screenshot above, which is perfectly fine.

Any events booked through Lawmatics where you are an attendee will be automatically placed onto the calendar chosen for ‘calendar to sync events’. If you are using our Appointment Request feature, clients will only be able to book you at times when you are free on all calendars selected in the ‘calendars to pull availability’ option.

We recommend enabling two-way sync. Two way sync will not send all events from your external calendar into Lawmatics. Rather, it will allow Lawmatics to reflect updates made externally.

So with two way sync enabled, if you make any edits to the appointment once it has been synced to your external calendar (such as rescheduling the time, adding a description, etc), these changes will be automatically updated in Lawmatics as well.

The rest of the settings on this page are only relevant if you are the using the Appointment Request feature. If so, feel free to set in your working hours, this will be used in addition to your existing appointments to set your availability.

You can also feel free to set in a lunch hour, buffer time, rolling period, and time before setting.

The time before setting will limit how soon you can be booked, if you want to be able to be booked same day, next day, 1 week out, or any other custom amount of time.

### B. CUSTOM CALENDAR BOOKING LINKS

Using our calendar booking feature is very easy within Lawmatics. However, sometimes there is a need to include a link to your calendar booking system from outside Lawmatics. For example, you may want to add a link to your website that allows perspective clients to easily book a consultation with you. This is simple with Lawmatics' calendar booking request custom links.

To create a custom link you must first have an event type created for the type of booking that you are seeking to give people access to. You event types are access from the settings page by clicking Event Settings from the left side navigation.

**Default Duration**

In order to be able to create a custom booking request link for an event type, you must first have a default duration for that event type. You can add default durations by simply clicking the pencil edit icon next to the desired event type.

**Getting Link**

Once you have added a default duration, and refreshed your screen if you added it at the same time, you will see an additional share icon on the right side of the event type. This icon is highlighted in the image below.

![](/img/3338087485477beb)

Simply click on that link for the event type you wish to create a booking request link for. Upon doing so, you will see the following options, explained below.

![](/img/e93380285d8af35e)

1. Choose the firm attendees who this appointment will be for. This indicates whose calendar will be pulled in for availability. You can also select more than one firm user. In that situation, we will combine the calendars and only offer times that both users are available.
2. Choose the location for this appointment. This is helpful if you need to create different links for different office locations. The link you generate will be specific to the location and the firm users that are specified in this form.
3. This is the unique link that will be linked the specified firm users and location. Copy this link and feel free to place it anywhere you like.

**Using the Link**

When someone clicks on the link to book an appointment on your calendar, they will first be prompted to enter their first name, last name and email address. If that person already exists in your Lawmatics database, we will link the new appointment to their matter. However, if they don't exist we will create a new matter in Lawmatics for you.

### C. BOOKING APPOINTMENTS

The first step in creating appointments is adding your event types. Event types label the different kinds of appointments your firm hosts, and allow you to trigger different automated workflows based on the type of event that is booked.

These event types are internal, and will not be visible to your clients. To give a few examples, your event types could be “Initial Consultation”, “Follow Up Appointment”, “Signing Meeting”, etc. You’ll create these event types in settings, in the Event Settings section.

You’ll also want to add in your firm’s address(es). These addresses will be available to select from when setting the location of the appointment.

You can add in your address in Firm Settings. First, you will click the Add Address button (pictured below), and then you’ll click Add Location, giving the address a label and selecting it from the list. You may also want to include an option for phone calls/teleconferences.

![](/img/eca9db16cac61a85)

Once you’ve created the event types and locations, you are ready to book an appointment. This can be done from the calendar (CRM -> Event Calendar) or from an individual matter.

![](/img/f45ec72a1d8285b0)

Remember that the appointment name is visible to the client, but the appointment type is not. Make sure to select the location, choose the attendees, enter a description if you wish, and choose the date and time.

You can set any of your users as the firm attendee(s), and if the attendee has synced their external calendar, the event will automatically appear on their synced calendar. Each user can manage their calendar sync in Calendar Settings.

You can also use our Appointment Request feature to let customers book their own appointments based on your availability. These requests can be sent via automation, from the matter, or you can also use our custom booking links found in Event Settings.

Once an appointment has been booked, you may want to have an automation set up to send a confirmation email/text. When you are drafting the email, remember, you can use the Event Fields to automatically merge in the date & time as well as location for the appointment.

![](/img/aa35268c797c0759)

## V. CONTACTS

### A. IMPORTING MATTERS & CONTACTS (*INCLUDING CUSTOM FIELD IMPORTS*)

1. The first step is to export your data from whatever system(s) you currently use to manage contacts. The vast majority of these programs should have an export function. If you have any trouble locating how to export from your current program, we encourage you to reach out to a support rep for the specific program you are using.

Once you’ve ran this export, you’ll have all of your data in a spreadsheet. This should include important
fields for each person like first name, last name, phone, email, etc. When importing into Lawmatics, it is
important to separate your contacts (referral sources, other attorneys, friends & family, etc) from your
matters (clients, prospects, and lost leads).

If you have any questions on what constitutes a contact vs. a matter, please take a look at our help article
titled Contacts vs. Matters before continuing. Please note that you most likely will not import anyone as a
'Client', you'll want to import your clients as matters with a Hired status. Keep reading for more information
on this.

2. The next step is to match the column headings on your spreadsheet to the headers that are allowed for
importing into Lawmatics. These field headers can be viewed by going to settings -> import, and then
selecting either Contact or Matter to see the allowed fields.

![](/img/610b53488000277b)

You will notice that there are more fields allowed for matters, since case related fields such as practice area, case title, etc. are included.

To help simplify this process of matching the column headings, we’ve provided a template for both matters and contacts. Please click below to open each template:

Matters: [Click Here](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1P8ht2jEq0_9-1PeDPTMAcV7AV25N-jVCgMOuWI5XJzY/edit?usp=sharing)

Contacts: [Click Here](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1qA88erCriJAiS2mk5u4oXnlihUAiobaVRFdccy2DLe0/edit?usp=sharing)
Feel free to copy and paste your data into the appropriate template if you find that simpler than changing the headings on your export.

**Importing Custom Field Data**

You can also import data to any of your custom fields in Lawmatics. This requires you to **already have the field created in Lawmatics, the import will not create new fields.**

To import to custom fields, you will need to uphold the following naming convention for custom fields:

field name(field type)

The field type will be either matter, contact, or practice_area. You also need to format the data properly. So if you're importing a date field, the data will need to be a date. If you're importing to a true/false field, the data will need to be either 'true' or 'false'.

For example, if you have the following custom fields in Lawmatics:

![](/img/4fbdc81f1f5c1ebc)

On your import spreadsheet, those fields would look like this:

![](/img/431947101e111f5f)

Since all three of these fields are Matter fields, they are labelled as such on the spreadsheet.

***Please note that the field names are case sensitive! You will need to match the field name on your spreadsheet exactly as it exists in Lawmatics.*

You'll see that since County was a picklist field, the spreadsheet uses allowed values from that picklist. Since Marriage date is a date field, the spreadsheet has dates for that field. And lastly, since Case closed is a true/false field, those are the values used.

If you are doing a contact import, you **can only use contact custom fields**. On matter imports, you **can import to contact,matter, or practice area custom fields**.

For more guidelines on importing other field types, make sure you read the Custom Field Notes found on the [import page](https://app.lawmatics.com/settings/import) of Lawmatics.
3. Once you have the correct headings on your spreadsheet for any of the fields you wish to include in the
import, you’ll want to sort through some of the data to make sure fields like 'practice area' and 'stage' match
what you have in Lawmatics.

Here are a few key notes:

- You will want to match the following fields to their values in Lawmatics. In parentheses you will find the location of each of these items in Lawmatics, so that you can view their values and match them on your spreadsheet.
- Contact Type (settings -> contact settings)
- Owned By (settings -> invite team)
- Stage (settings -> stage settings)
- Practice Area (settings -> practice areas)
- Source (settings -> marketing settings, the source will be the main heading)
- Campaign (settings -> marketing settings, the campaign is found under a source)
- If they do not match the existing values, a new value will be created. This can be useful, or it may be undesirable.
- For example, you may have created a practice area in Lawmatics called ‘Bankruptcy - Ch. 7’. If you import a matter with the practice area labeled as ‘BK - Chapter 7’, it will create a new practice area rather than assigning it to the existing. This would be undesirable, because you would have duplicate practice areas.
- To give an example of when this can be useful, if you have practice areas on your spreadsheet that you did not take the time to create in Lawmatics, the import will create them for you. The same is true for any of the fields listed above.

It is also important to note that not all of the fields you see in the templates (or on the import page in settings) are required. The only required field is First Name, the rest are up to you whether you want to include them or not.

Another important field that you should pay attention to is the status. This field only applies to matter imports, not contact imports, and it will tell Lawmatics whether each matter is a PNC, Hired client, or Lost lead. The only allowed values in this column are: PNC, Hired, and Lost. It is important to match one of these three options for all matters in order import them with the correct status.
4. You are almost ready to import your data. Before importing, make sure you have checked all of the
following:

- Are contacts and matters separated onto two different spreadsheets?
- Are all column headings labeled properly?
- Have you made sure there are no extra column headings that do not match the allowed columns? Remember that matters have more allowed fields than contacts.
- Are any custom fields that you are importing already created in Lawmatics?
- Do you have custom fields labelled correctly as per the required naming convention?
- Are you only using 'matter' or 'practice area' type custom fields on matter imports?
- Do all entries have a first name?
- Do all practice areas and stages match what is existing in Lawmatics?
- If not, are you happy with the new ones that will be created?
- Do all contact types match what is existing in Lawmatics?
- If not, are you happy with the new ones that will be created?
- Do all marketing sources and campaigns match what is existing in Lawmatics?
- If not, are you happy with the new ones that will be created?
- IMPORTANT LAST STEP: Is the file saved as the following file type: CSV UTF-8 (Comma Delimited) (.csv)

5. Once you have checked all of the boxes above, you are ready to import.
In Lawmatics, navigate to settings -> import. At the bottom, you will see a button for ‘Import Data’. If you are importing both matters and contacts, they will be imported separately. You will want to do matters first, so select that as the type, and then select your CSV file. Once you’ve done so, the Run Import button that is greyed out in the screenshot below will turn green, and you can select it.

![](/img/9a08c8116dd586c9)

Then, while that import is processing, you will click the ‘Import Data’ button at the bottom once again, choose Contact as the type, select your contact spreadsheet, and click Run Import.
6. Finally, you will need to be patient as your files import. Depending on the size, it may take some time. You
will receive an email notifying you when the import is complete.

### B. CONTACTS v. MATTERS

Contacts in Lawmatics are referring to a person, whereas Matters are referring to a case. Every Matter will have at least one corresponding Contact, but not every Contact will necessarily have a Matter. Contacts who would not have a corresponding matter would be referral sources, other attorneys, friends & family, etc. These people are still important to have in the CRM, but they are not necessarily clients or prospective clients, and therefore, they would not have a matter.

When you create a new matter, this will include creating a new contact to be linked to that matter, or selecting from your already existing contacts. Whether you create a new contact or select from existing, this contact will be linked to the Matter.

The image below is what you will see when you are creating a new matter. Selecting the blue button for Add New Contact will bring up fields for you to enter the person’s first name, last name, email, phone, etc. Clicking on the Search Contact box at the bottom will bring a drop down list of all your existing contacts in Lawmatics for you to select from.

![](/img/97debc8e9a892261)

If the same contact comes to your firm with separate matters, you will only need to create the contact once, and then you can link that contact to more than one matter.

You will also notice as you are creating objects such as forms, documents, and emails in Lawmatics, you will have the option to select a type. If the object is case related, for example an intake form, retainer agreement, consultation confirmation email, etc, then the type should be Matter.

If you are creating marketing content that could be used for any contact, not just matters, then the type should be Contact.

When you are using the search bar (magnifying glass in the top right) to locate a contact or a matter, you will see an icon next to each search result. The icon with three people represents the matter, and the icon with a card represents the contact. In the image below, you’ll see the first result is the matter, showing the linked contact’s name in bold, and the title of the case in parentheses. The second result is the contact.

![](/img/a918e1412952af02)

If you’re looking for anything related to the case, like the activity timeline, notes, tasks, appointments, etc, then you will select the Matter from these search results.

It is important to note that every matter in Lawmatics will have a status of either PNC, Hired, or Lost. PNCs are your prospects/leads, Hired Matters are your current and past clients, and Lost Matters are PNCs that did not end up converting for whatever reason.

When you hover over the CRM tab in the top left of Lawmatics, you’ll see options for both Matters and Contacts. When you select Matters, there are some useful Saved Filtered Views on the left. These filtered views break up your matters by the statuses listed above.

When you hover on the CRM tab and select Contact, you will notice a column titled Type, just to the right of the Email column. Any contacts that are linked to a matter will have a type of Client or PNC Contact, depending on the matter’s status.

You can create custom Contact Types to label your non-matter contacts appropriately, for example you might have types for Referral Source, Colleague, etc. These contact types can be created by going to settings -> contact settings.

Once you’ve created your custom contact types, you can assign them to contacts by opening up the contact, and clicking the edit pencil under their name, as shown in the image below. In this example, the custom contact type is Attorney.
