## VI. MATTERS

### A. CREATING MATTERS

Adding matters is one of the key actions you will be doing in Lawmatics. Matters can be created any of the following ways:

1. **From a custom form**
2. **From the quick add button in Lawmatics**
3. **From the matters page on the CRM**
4. **From the Lawmatics dashboard**
5. **From an event type appointment request link**

We’ll be going in depth on each of these different methods to create a matter. Before moving forward, we also recommend that you first read our article on matters vs. contacts.

**1. Creating a matter from a custom form**

One of the main benefits of using custom forms to create matters is that you have complete customization over what fields you want to capture. You can build any of our standard fields and any of your custom fields into a custom form. This allows you to capture any and all information that is essential for your intake right in one place.

When you create a custom form you will need to select the form type of either contact or matter. This determines what will be created when the form is submitted, so in the case of intake forms, you’ll want the type to be matter.

We suggest creating a custom form to be used for Phone Intake. This form can act as a script for whoever is taking inbound calls at your firm and allows them to take down all necessary information and create the matter with one click. You can also make this form internal so that you have access to internal fields like marketing source, pipeline stage, etc.

You will also want to create a form to embed on your website. Embedding this form on your site will result in a new matter automatically being created in Lawmatics each time a new lead fills out the form.

Remember, you can also trigger any automations off a form being filled. This means that you can trigger different actions if a matter came from the ‘phone intake form’ rather than the ‘web form’.

**2. Lawmatics quick add button**

When you are in Lawmatics you will notice an orange plus sign in the very top right corner. Hovering over this icon will bring up a number of quick actions, you’ll select New Matter to create a matter.

This will bring up our standard create matter box. Here you will be able to assign a practice area, owner, case title, pipeline stage, and fill in the contact details for this matter. You can also select from existing contacts if this is a return client.

Creating a matter this way will put the matter on your pipeline at whichever stage you have selected. You can then pull up the matter to share any forms, edit any additional fields, etc.

**3. Matters page within the CRM**

When you hover over the CRM tab found in the top left of Lawmatics, you will see an option for Matters. Clicking on Matters will bring up all of your matters, filtered on the left side of the screen by status.

You will notice a button to Add Matter at the bottom of this page. Selecting this option will bring up the same create matter box that you would see if you created a matter from the orange plus sign.

**4. Lawmatics Dashboard**

You can access the dashboard at any point by clicking on the Lawmatics logo in the very top left. Here you will find a number of quick actions and stats at a glance. One of the options found in the Quick Actions section at the very top is New Matter.

This will open the same create matter box that we have discussed in the last two methods of creating a matter.

**5. Custom event booking link**

You can use our custom booking links to simultaneously schedule an appointment with a new lead and create them as a matter in Lawmatics. This feature lets the PNC choose their own appointment based on your availability. In order to use this feature, you will need to have an external calendar synced (settings -> calendar settings).

To create a booking link, you’ll go to settings -> event settings. Here you can create custom event types for your firm like “Initial Consultation” or “Follow Up Meeting”, etc. Once you have created the event types and given each a default duration, you will see an icon on the right with an arrow. Use this icon to generate the booking link, determining whichever users and locations you would like to include for the meeting.

You can then share this link via email or embed it on your website. When a PNC clicks the link, they will need to fill in their name and email before they can book an appointment. When they do so, their matter will be automatically created in Lawmatics along with the scheduled appointment time that they've chosen.

### B. MATTER TAGGING

***Please note: Matter tags and Contact tags are different. Contact tags live on the contact and matter tags live on the matter. Contact tags will be visible from the matter details page under contact information. Matter tags will not be visible from a contact's details page. If you add a tag to a matter, it WILL NOT apply to the contact. The same applies the opposite way. If you apply a tag to a contact, it will not apply the same tag to the matter.*

Adding tags to matters can be done in two different ways.
**1. Matter Details page.**

Simple navigate to a matter, click on Edit in the bottom of the screen, and then you will see a field for Tags under the Matter Information heading.

![](/img/941c164d4a5a8738)

From here, you can add new tags to the matter AND you can create new tags. Simply begin typing the tag you would like to add then press enter, this will create a new tag in the system and apply that tag to the Matter once you click Save at bottom of screen.

You can even change the color of a tag from this edit view. Click on the tag and you will be given a color selector as seen in the image below.

![](/img/e9f25929d9070dcd)

**2. Automations**

You can also add tags to matters via automations. This is accomplished using the Change Attribute action in an automation sequence. In order to apply tags to matters via automations, select the Tags(Matters) field from the change attributes drop down. Then, select the tags that you would like to have applied when this automation action fires. You can also add tags on this screen.

![](/img/059f649609702e70)

### C. ESTIMATED VALUE v ACTUAL VALUE

Lawmatics has two different native fields designed to capture the monetary value associated with matters. This article will explain the difference between the two.

At its most basic level, Estimated Value is meant to capture the expected revenue that will be generated from a matter. This is best used during the intake phase, before a lead has hired your firm. Actual Value is meant to hold the actual amount of revenue that you received in the matter. This is something that should be entered after the case is completely over.

**Estimated Value**

As previously mentioned, estimated value is meant to capture the anticipated value of a matter. Perhaps you have a personal injury lead that was involved in a car accident. You might have an idea what you think the case is worth. You also know what fee percentage you would be taking in the case. It would be appropriate to add this expected firm revenue to the estimated value field.

The estimated value field will be used primarily on the Pipeline page. Lawmatics will use the estimated value numbers to give you revenue projections from each stage of your process that is represented with a pipeline stage. This is designed to give you a rough estimate of the amount of revenue that you have sitting in your pipeline. You can also use estimated value in custom reports in order to view this data in the way that you want to see it.

**Actual Value**

Actual Value is specifically designed to receive the total revenue that your firm generated from a particular matter. For that reason, it is typically a number that is added into Lawmatics only when a matter is completely closed out, or when all money has been received on the matter. It is important to populate this field whenever possible though as the number is a critical piece to the ROI (Return on Investment) reporting that is built into Lawmatics. Actual Value can also be used in custom reporting the same way that Estimate Value can. Currently, Actual Value is a field that must be manually updated, it does not auto populate with data from your practice management solution.

### D. ASSIGNED STAFF PERMISSION LEVEL

The Assigned Staff field allows you to set permission levels limiting your firm Lawmatics users to only view matters that they are assigned to.

To set this permission level, go to Settings > Manage Users > Manage Roles. Note: if you do not see the Manage Users option in settings, your user status may not have permission to view that page.

Once you click Manage Roles (found in the top right on the Mange Users page), you can create a new role or edit any of your existing roles.

Under the Access to Matters section, check the box labelled hey are Assigned Staff to limit the role access to only be able to view matters that they are assigned to.

![](/img/a63f41c9bc84002f)

To select which users are assigned to a matter, you will need to populate them in the Assigned Staff field. To find this field, go to the matter profile, select the Details tab, and then you'll find it in the Matter Information section. Click the Edit button at the bottom right to populate the field.

![](/img/7dbdb3707cae361d)

This field will show a dropdown list of all of your firm Lawmatics users. Feel free to select as many users as you wish to assign to the matter, you are not limited to just one user in this field.

![](/img/98df401523886b2a)

## VII. CUSTOM FIELDS

### A. CUSTOM FIELD OVERVIEW (VIDEO)

[Watch here](https://help.lawmatics.com/article/168-video-custom-field-overview)

## VIII. TASKS (VIDEO)

[Watch here](https://help.lawmatics.com/category/186-tasks)

## IX. REPORTING

### A. TRACKING ROI

**SPEND**

Spend is entered on the marketing settings page, and it can be entered on a monthly, weekly, or daily level. Whenever possible, we recommend tracking Spend on a daily basis. Sources like Google PPC or Facebook Ads make it very easy to see how much money you spend each day.

**Follow these steps to enter spend:**

1. Navigate to Settings > Marketing Settings2. Locate the source and campaign that you are entering Spend for. Click on the dollar sign icon in order to bring up the Spend form.

![](/img/8b2d432852f2503f)

2. Select the date or date range (week or month) and enter the amount of Spend for that period.

**REVENUE**

The other critical number that is needed to calculate ROI is the Total Revenue generated from a matter. In order to track Revenue, you must use the **ACTUAL REVENUE** field on the matter. This is a field we provide you, so no need to create anything new.

It is important to make sure this number reflects the TOTAL amount of revenue you received from a matter. You can update this field as often as you want — you can record revenue on a matter as it comes in. This is a manual field you need to fill in.

**ROI Calculation**

Here is an example of how ROI would be calculated in Lawmatics. For this example we have the following data:

- Source "Google PPC" with spend for March of $2,000.
- Our firm received 10 leads in March.
- 2 of those leads from March hired our firm.
- In June we closed the cases and had a total revenue of $10,000

If we use the ROI tracker to review the ROI for March, we will see an ROI of 500%. **When** the person hires the firm is irrelevant to the ROI calculation. We care about when the lead came in and how much money was spent on marketing to acquire that lead compared to the revenue generated from any leads that came in during the same period and hired the firm.

### B. CUSTOM REPORTING (VIDEO)

[Watch here](https://help.lawmatics.com/article/174-custom-reportingvideo)

## X. FILE REQUEST TEMPLATES

File Request Templates allow you to collect necessary files and documents from your clients electronically with ease. This functions as a client portal of sorts, where clients can upload their files, and you’ll receive them automatically on their matter in Lawmatics.

You’ll find this feature by hovering over the Assets tab, and then selecting File Requests. Start by clicking Create File Request Template. You will see a window similar to the image below. Give your template a name, an email subject and message, and list the requested file(s).

![](/img/1afafeb3c287d8fe)

Your template can have as many files as you wish. If you’ve checked the box for “Allow requestee” to upload additional optional files” then your clients will have an additional space to upload any additional files that are not specified on the list.

Once you’ve saved your template, you will see it in the File Request Templates Section. You can send any of these templates by clicking the envelope icon, circled below. Once you have sent out a file request, you’ll see it listed under File Requests, along with which matter (requestee) it was sent to.

![](/img/d2bba3a286947122)

You can also build file requests into an automation, rather than manually sending them using the button above. When you add an action to an automation you will see an option for Request Files.

When your client receives the request from you and clicks on the link in the email, this is what they will see:

![](/img/7df30b14aef5c501)

They can click on each section to browse their files, or simply drag and drop a file into the appropriate section. Once they have included the required files they can click upload files, they will then receive a message that their files were successfully submitted.

If you want to be notified of file submissions, you can turn on the notification for that by going to settings, notifications. Each user at your firm also has the option to turn on this notification.

Any files uploaded by your clients will automatically be saved directly to the Files tab on their matter, where you can then download them if necessary.

![](/img/3f51a40945cf3d9a)

You can also use the action of files being uploaded to trigger an automation, so if you want to initiate the next step in your process once you’ve received their files, you can have that happen automatically by selecting the trigger for Requested File.

![](/img/661f76c071fad367)

***Article source: https://help.lawmatics.com/ ***

pages.title: How to conduct Client-VA Onboarding
pages.summary: Client VA onboarding helps us to have a successful transition. This is when we initially introduce the VA to his/her client. We can ask the client for their expectations and necessary instructions to make sure that th…
pages.body:
Client - VA onboarding helps us to have a successful transition. This is when we initially introduce the VA to his/her client. We can ask the client for their expectations and necessary instructions to make sure that the VA performs the tasks assigned to him/her with a good outcome.

This is conducted via Zoom or Google Meet hosted by the assigned POC.

**The flow of discussion:**

1. **Team Introduction **

- Greetings to the attorney
- Introduce present officers

- * (Note: Orient VA about the flow of discussion to avoid unpleasant experiences. It's like we are preparing
them for their interview)*

2. **VA Introduction (*Remember the First impression last and tone of voice matters. Feel happy that you have a new client!)***
- Introduce yourself and share previous work experiences that are related to the role.
- If with experience, share how long you've been a VA and what type of law firm/business.
- If new VA, VA had training and internship with a Personal Injury Law Firm.
- Share your skill proficiencies
- Close introduction with excitement but do not over-promise.

3.** Questions for the client:**

- What are the expectations from the VA?
- What are the do's and don'ts or firms' policies that the VA should follow?
- Does the VA need to use separate trackers aside from the one we already have?

4. Credentials
- Work email
- CRM
- Softphone
- Storage
- Communication (Skype, Slack, hangouts, etc)

5. When is the official starting date of the VA? Official business hours
6. Will it be part-time or full-time? If part-time, what specific time in a day do they need the VA?

If w/other client disclose to set the proper expectation that full-time VAs tracked minimum of 8 hours, since VA only track hours whenever there are tasks to complete we also ensure they have enough task, we can always eventually make VA full-time for 1 client

7. Any other specific instructions/documents to endorse like confidentiality agreement
8. Remind the client that invoice coverage is 2 weeks from the official start date.

pages.title: CMS - Clio Grow
pages.summary: Clio’s cloud based client intake and legal client relationship management (CRM) software transforms the way your firm attracts and retains prospective clients.
pages.body:
![](/img/d310e2ad4febe270)

Clio’s cloud-based client intake and legal client relationship management (CRM) software transforms the way your firm attracts and retains prospective clients.

# 1. Attract and retain new clients online—even while working remotely

## Automate your intake process

![](/img/9fce4880cd9c242f)

Use shareable, online intake forms, e-signatures, and document automation to turn your firm’s client intake process into a simple, organized system in the cloud.

## Schedule consultations and accept payments online

![](/img/4f030c9d2c847c88)

Enable effortless appointment booking with Clio Scheduler—and integrate it with Clio Manage’s Payments functionality to accept payment before you meet and reduce the risk of no-shows.

## Automate redundant tasks, emails, and workflows

![](/img/d95118555b0b71f5)

Streamline day-to-day tasks like email follow-up and data entry, lowering overhead and freeing up time for more profitable tasks—so you can focus on what matters most.

# 2. Legal Client Relationship Management (CRM)

## A. Client management

Manage your contacts and email lists with a cloud-based legal CRM to ensure that no relationship or business opportunity falls through the cracks.

## B. Automate your most important tasks

“Set and forget” essential aspects of client retention and communication—like client intake, appointment reminders and email follow-ups.

### Standardize the client intake process

Automate client intake workflows to ensure no communication or billable opportunity gets missed.

![](/img/44d4e982f4312273)

- Know where potential clients are in the intake process - Get real-time status updates on matters, client appointments, and pending requests with a comprehensive Matter Pipeline and agenda.
- Secure new clients in one click - Bring in potential clients and open new matters rapidly with a Quick Intake button that automates each step.

### Customize work, task, and email templates

Build step-by-step templates that you and your staff can use to complete repetitive work efficiently.

![](/img/2c1cbc9c936d107a)

- Organize your firm’s processes - Keep new cases organized and better manage firm workflows by filtering matters by status, type, location, and more.
- Account for every detail - Improve your client intake process with checklists that keep tasks, emails, and appointments in order—and on track.

- Create, schedule, and send automated-yet-personalized client communications -
Use unlimited email templates, timed-delivery email scheduling, and automated reminders to keep potential and current clients in the loop.

## C. Onboard and manage clients with ease

![](/img/e98b603fb9ab9209)

1. Know the status of every client at a glance - See the current status of each potential or retained client. Get an overview of their contact and matter details from an easy-to-understand dashboard.
2. Organize contacts with customizable tags - Tag and categorize potential clients, existing clients, and professional contacts in our legal CRM software, so you can find who you need, when you need them.
3. Cut down on consultation no-shows - Simplify the appointment scheduling process and automate sending appointment reminders to clients.

## D. Make great client experiences your differentiator

Turn every potential client into a referral, a good review, and more business for your law firm.

1. Never miss a client follow-up - Use our legal CRM software to automatically create tasks and reminders that will ensure you’re keeping clients in the loop at every stage of their client intake journey.
2. Run automated email campaigns - Create tailored, multi-step email campaigns that engage your new and incoming clients through the client intake process.
3. Impress with seamless client engagement - Build a CRM workflow that’s easy for you and your clients, including customized online intake forms, instant document creation, and e-signatures.

## E. Get actionable insights on how to grow your firm

Get easy-to-understand reporting from our legal CRM software. See how your law firm’s marketing and business development efforts are performing.

1. Get an overview of incoming clients - Convert more clients using our legal CRM software. See where in the intake process each potential new client is at using a visualized ‘Matter Pipeline’ and get updates as they progress to being a case.
2. Know where to market your firm - Know where new clients are learning about your firm so you can focus your marketing efforts. Get a report on who referred new clients to your firm, and how their referrals translated into retained clients.
3. Recognize your high value clients - Know the incoming number and value of new clients, broken down by practice area.

# 4. Document Automation & Electronic Signatures

Legally-binding documents, forms, and agreements—created, signed, and stored online.

![](/img/7e8c80e08526bd7f)

## A. Make document signing easier

Take the complexity out of document signing and sending with easy, fast e-signatures and ready-to-share custom documents and agreements.

1. Save everyone’s time—including your own - Approve information in moments—not hours—and move cases along faster.
2. Be more efficient with everything in one place - Automated document creation and integrated e-signature technology remove the need to purchase additional software, printers, paper, and more.
3. Speed up the client intake process - Send documents securely to clients in seconds and receive notifications about new signatures to remove bottlenecks during the intake process.

## B. Securely store, work on, and share client documents in the cloud

Secure logins allow you to review, sign, and work on client documents from anywhere with mobile-friendly technology.

1. Make creating, sending, and signing a document as easy as 1-2-3 - Send newly secured clients ready-made agreements or retainers, and have them signed and sent back to you quickly with e-signatures.
2. Enable client intake on the go with Clio Grow’s mobile e-signature functions - Your clients can sign legal documents on their phones and tablets and send them back to you, hassle-free.
3. Remove the risk of human error - No need to download, print, or send forms via snail mail. Your clients can securely sign and return forms as needed, all online.

# 5. Client Intake Insights Software

Get reporting on your firm’s client intake process. Identify who your best potential clients are, how they find you, and what you can do to bring in more revenue.

## A. See the data behind your firm’s performance

Get in-depth client intake reporting on what’s driving revenue and boosting productivity from an easy-to-use dashboard—the more you know, the more you can do.

![](/img/77ed31997e96a58a)

1. Identify opportunities to grow your firm - Focus on the most profitable practice areas, matter types, and clients for your firm by analyzing the right data.
2. Track and highlight key revenue sources - Identify top-performing firm members, referral sources, and client types to improve your law firm’s profitability.
3. Get a view into firm financials from the start - Estimate initial matter values, and update estimates as you retain new clients for better financial forecasting.
4. Customize reports to fit your practice needs - Filter data for detailed information on matter types, lead sources, staff members, and more. Structure client intake reports so they make sense for your firm.

## B. Set smarter goals to achieve better results

Find out where your firm should be headed—and how to get there—by seeing what works and what doesn’t.

1. Find out why clients hire you - Monitor what causes clients to sign with your firm, as opposed to a competitor.
2. Set more accurate revenue targets - Analyze your pipeline to learn which services and marketing efforts are your top earners—and which ones aren’t pulling their weight.

# 6. Appointment Booking

Deliver the effortless experience clients expect while automating your firm’s intake process with Clio Scheduler. Make it easy for prospective clients to book, pay for, and confirm their appointments with you in the cloud.

![](/img/a5f649c48768ed0b)

## A. Make booking appointments online a breeze

Enjoy appointment booking in the cloud that’s convenient for everyone—you, your firm, and your clients. Reduce the risk of no-shows, automate your client intake process, guarantee payment, and save time.

1. Stay in control of your calendar - Booking preferences mean you can prevent same day, back-to-back, or last minute appointment bookings. Optimize your day and get back the time you need to leave new clients with a great first impression.
2. Reduce the friction of booking and rescheduling appointments - Manage your schedule in a way that works for you by offering available time slots in your calendar—fully accessible from an easy-to-use online booking page.
3. Deliver a better client experience—in the cloud - Offer a modern, hassle-free online booking experience with easy payment options and automated appointment confirmations and reminders.

## B. Offer an online appointment booking system that works for your firm

Clio Scheduler makes it easy to connect with and schedule in new clients while offering a consistently great client experience with your firm—from anywhere, at any time.

1. Accept electronic credit card payments online - Combine Clio Scheduler with [Clio Payments](https://www.clio.com/features/payments/) in Clio Manage—so clients can pay you the way they prefer: instantly and securely, via credit card. All in the cloud, with a few simple clicks.
2. Integrate Clio’s legal appointment booking software with tools you already use - Keep record-keeping consistent across your entire firm. Clio Scheduler enables events and appointments to appear automatically in your Outlook and Google calendars.
3. Keep intake details in one central, cloud-based system - Take advantage of the Clio Suite and sync Clio Scheduler with Clio Manage, so you can accept electronic credit card payments, and integrate your calendars with Outlook or Google. Avoid double bookings, manual data entry, and save time.
4. Add Clio Scheduler to Google My Business and turn Google searches into clients - Potential clients can book appointments right from your [Business Profile in Google](https://www.clio.com/features/integrations/google/) with Clio Scheduler. Once an appointment is booked, a lead is added to Clio Grow making intake even easier.

# How to & References:

### I. Overview

[Grow 1: Start using clio grow today](https://fast.wistia.net/embed/channel/am3vp3c35j?wchannelid=am3vp3c35j&wmediaid=xx1q0kcrjt)

[Grow 2: Seamless scheduling and matter management with clio suite](https://fast.wistia.net/embed/channel/am3vp3c35j?wchannelid=am3vp3c35j&wmediaid=ib91cihi7o)

[Clio grow overview webinar](https://fast.wistia.net/embed/channel/am3vp3c35j?wchannelid=am3vp3c35j&wmediaid=d295a8rp3h)

[Clio grow overview](https://fast.wistia.net/embed/channel/am3vp3c35j?wchannelid=am3vp3c35j&wmediaid=c2g584kdq7)

### II. Administrative and Account setup

[How to setup your clio grow account overview](https://fast.wistia.net/embed/channel/am3vp3c35j?wchannelid=am3vp3c35j&wmediaid=cr43r8m4j4)

[How to connect clio grow with clio practice management](https://fast.wistia.net/embed/channel/am3vp3c35j?wchannelid=am3vp3c35j&wmediaid=nwmxy7a329)

[How to configure matter settings](https://fast.wistia.net/embed/channel/am3vp3c35j?wchannelid=am3vp3c35j&wmediaid=n9r1s4xvlq)

How to configure your contact settings

### III. Intake and lead Management

pages.title: FAMILY LAW
pages.summary: Family law is a legal practice area that focuses on issues involving family relationships, such as adoption , divorce , and child custody , among others. Attorneys practicing family law can represent clients in family…
pages.body:
***Family law*** is a legal practice area that focuses on issues involving family relationships, such as *adoption*, *divorce*, and *child custody*, among others. Attorneys practicing family law can represent clients in family court proceedings or in related negotiations and can also draft important legal documents such as *court petitions* or *property agreements*. Some family law attorneys even specialize in *adoption*, *paternity*, *emancipation*, or other matters not usually related to divorce.

**Family Law Process Flowchart:**

![](/img/146ca121ad377b84)

**A. DIVORCE, LEGAL SEPARATION, AND ANNULMENT**
Ø ***File*** Petition and Summons - if children ***file*** UCCJEA (Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement Act)
Ø ***Serve*** Petition and Summons - if children ***serve*** UCCJEA (Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and
Enforcement Act)

**DIVORCE**
**First Steps for Divorce**
Your first step should be to consult an experienced divorce attorney. Even if you have not fully made a decision, they can help you to understand what the likely outcomes may be in terms of financial and custody arrangements.
**LEGAL SEPARATION**
If you choose to separate from your spouse before divorce, you will want to keep in mind the legal implications of separation. There are three kinds of separation: trial separation, permanent separation, and legal separation.
**TRIAL SEPARATION**

Describes spouses living apart while deciding whether or not to divorce. Depending on the length of the separation, trial separation may have no effect on property rights during a divorce.
**PERMANENT SEPARATION**

Describes spouses living apart after deciding to end their marriage. Generally, property and debts acquired after the date of permanent separation are assigned to the spouse who acquired them.
**LEGAL SEPARATION**

Is a formal state of separation awarded by a family court. Spouses who have legally separated are no longer married, but they are not divorced and not free to remarry. Legal separation can function as an alternative to divorce in some states.
**RESIDENCE AND CHILDREN **
If there are children from the marriage and you live separately, you will need to work out some kind of provisional custody agreement. Generally, attorneys will advise you to give your spouse reasonable access to the children, barring any safety or other serious concerns.

**B. IMMEDIATE ORDERS NEEDED AND FILE ORDER TO SHOW CAUSE: **
· Child Custody
· Visitation
· Support
· Property
· Restraining Orders
**I.CHILD CUSTODY **
**Two kinds of Child Custody**
1. ***Legal custody,*** which means who makes important decisions for your children (like health care, education, and welfare). Parents with ***legal custody*** make decisions or choices about their children’s:
· School or child care

· Religious activities or institutions
· Psychiatric, psychological, or other mental health counseling or therapy needs
· Doctor, dentist, orthodontist, or other health professionals (except in emergency situations)
· Sports, summer camp, vacation, or extracurricular activities
· Travel
· Residence (where the children will live)
2. ***Physical custody,*** which means who your children live with and can be:
· Joint, which means that the children live with both parents.
· Sole or primary, which means the children live with 1 parent most of the time and usually visit the other parent.
**II.VISITATION ORDER**
Visitation orders are varied, depending on the best interests of the children, the situation of the parents, and other factors. In general, visitation can be:
· **Visitation according to a schedule:** It helps the parents and children to have detailed visitation plans to prevent conflicts and confusion, so parents and courts often come up with a visitation schedule detailing the dates and times that the children will be with each parent. Visitation schedules can include holidays, special occasions (like birthdays, mother's day, father's day, and other
important dates for the family), and vacations.
· **Reasonable visitation:** It does not necessarily have details as to when the children
will be with each parent. Usually, these orders are open-ended and allow the
parents to work it out between them. This type of visitation plan can work if parents
get along very well and can be flexible and communicate well with one another.
But if there are ever disagreements or misunderstandings, this kind of an open
schedule can cause issues between the parents, and the children may suffer as a
result.
· **Supervised visitation:** This is used when the children’s safety and well-being require
that visits with the other parent be supervised by you, another adult, or a professional agency. sometimes also used in cases where a child and a parent need time to become more familiar with each other, like if a parent has not seen the child in a long time and they need to slowly get to know each other again.
· **No visitation:** This option is used when visiting with the parent, even with supervision, would be physically or emotionally harmful to the children. In these cases, it is not in the best interest of the children for the parent to have any contact with the children.

**III.CHILD SUPPORT **
***Child support*** is the amount of money that a court orders a parent or both parents to pay every month to help pay for the support of the child (or children) and the child’s living expenses.
· Prepare forms;
· Explain court procedures for getting and changing child support orders;
· Calculate child support using the guideline if you have the necessary financial information; and
· Explain how the court makes child support decisions.
**IV.RESTRAINING ORDER**
A ***restraining order*** can be both temporary or permanent. If the order is temporary, it's a short-term order. A temporary order aims to protect an individual until there is a subsequent or final hearing. Typically, these orders last from five days to two weeks but may last longer depending on the next hearings' date.

**C. Hearing and Order Hearing**
**RESPONSE FILED?**
**YES - Voluntary Settlement Conference **
A **settlement conference** is an opportunity for the parties in a case to discuss issues and make their own decisions as to how to resolve these issues while meeting with a judge who will not preside over the trial in their case if a trial is still required.
In general, voluntary settlement conferences are similar to mediations. Unlike mediation, where the parties negotiate their preferred settlement terms, in a voluntary settlement conference, the attorneys for each side actively negotiate the terms of a possible settlement.
**NO - Default Process File documents for default judgment**

**D. AGREEMENT?**
**What happens if we AGREE?
**Settlement Stipulated Judgement or Judgment with Marital Settlement Agreement attached.
A **Stipulated Judgment** is similar to a Marital Settlement Agreement in that the Stipulated Judgment contains agreements between the parties about all of the same issues discussed above. However, a Stipulated Judgment is usually a shorter and more abbreviated version of a Marital Settlement Agreement.
**E. Declaration Regarding Service of Declaration of Disclosure and Income and Expense Declaration filed?**
**NO**
No action by the court until Declaration Regarding Service of Declaration of Disclosure and Income & Expense Declaration is filed.
**YES**

**1. File Request for Status Conference to Set Case for Trial form**
If both you and the other party have filed, the Petition and Response and your divorce case still are not finished. If you or the other party just recently filed the Response, wait and give the court time to schedule a hearing called a “Case Management Conference”. However, if it has been a while since the Response was filed and the Court has not scheduled a Case Management Conference or a Mandatory Settlement Conference hearing, then you can file a Request for Trial.
**2. Status Conference Hearing date set**
**3. File Case Status Questionnaire 4 days before Case Status Conference**

**F. Case Status Conference Case Settled?**
**YES**
**SETTLEMENT:**
Stipulated Judgement or Judgement with Marital Settlement Agreement attached
**What happens if we DO NOT AGREE? **
· 15 days prior to Settlement Conference face-to-face meeting required 5.45(b) (Local Rules)
· Set for mandatory Settlement Conference Statement 5 days before the conference
· If case Status Conference Case **settled** – Settlement: Stipulated Judgment or Judgement with Marital Settlement Agreement attached.
· If case Status Conference Case **Not Settled** – will proceed to **TRIAL**

pages.title: ESTATE PLANNING
pages.summary: Estate planning is a process involving the counsel of professional advisors who are familiar with your goals and concerns, your assets and how they are owned, and your family structure. It can involve the services of …
pages.body:
**Estate planning** is a process involving the counsel of professional advisors who are familiar with your goals and concerns, your assets and how they are owned, and your family structure. It can involve
the services of a variety of professionals, including your lawyer, accountant,
financial planner, life insurance advisor, banker, and a broker.
Estate planning covers the transfer of property at death as well as a variety of other personal matters and may or may not involve tax planning. The core document most often associated with this process is your will.
*Will – A writing specifying the beneficiaries who are to inherit the testator’s assets and naming a representative to administer the estate and be responsible for distributing the assets to the beneficiaries.*
That is **estate planning**—making a plan in advance, naming the people or organizations you want to receive the things you own after you die, and taking steps now to make carrying out your plan as easy
as possible later. However, good estate planning is much more than that. It should also do the following:
· include instructions for your care and financial affairs if you become incapacitated
before you die
· include arrangements for disability income insurance to replace your income if you cannot work due to illness or injury, long-term care insurance to help pay for your care in case of an extended illness or injury, and life insurance to provide for your family at your death
· provide for the transfer of your business at your retirement, disability, incapacity, or death
· name a guardian for your minor children’s care and inheritance
· provide for family members with special needs without disqualifying them from government benefits
· provide for loved ones who might be irresponsible with money or who may need protection
from creditors or in the event of divorce
· minimize taxes, court costs, and unnecessary legal fees, which may include funding assets into a living trust, completing or updating beneficiary designations, or otherwise aligning your assets with your estate plan
**If You Do Not Have a Plan, Your State Has One For You—But You Might Not Like It**

**At disability:** If your name is on the title of your assets and you cannot conduct business due to mental or physical incapacity, only someone appointed by a court can sign for you. The court will supervise and ultimately control how your assets are used for your care through a conservatorship or guardianship (depending on the term used in your state). It can become expensive and time-consuming, it is of public record to some extent, and it can be difficult to end even if you recover.
**At your death:** If you die without a valid estate plan, any assets owned in your individual name and without a beneficiary designation or other governing contract will be distributed according to your
state’s intestacy laws, typically through a court-supervised probate proceeding. In many states, if you are married and have children, your spouse and children will each receive a share, even if your children are from a prior marriage or no longer minors. That means your spouse could receive only a fraction of your estate, which may not be enough to live on. If you have minor children, the court will control their inheritance. If both parents die (e.g., in a car accident), the court will appoint a guardian without knowing whom you would have chosen.

**ESTATE PLANNING FLOW CHART**

![](/img/36be731a87ea9ce3)

**Have you located the will? **
**NO**
Ø **Choose who the administrator will be**

- Someone who is ***willing***, able to do the work, and ***familiar*** with your unique situation. Typically, this ends up being an immediate family member or close friend.

Ø **Make your application for letters of administration**
- You need ***Letters of Administration*** to begin closing a deceased person’s estate. This document will give you permission to access their finances and assets, and manage them according to

state law (Or the Will if there is one). For example, most financial institutions will require you to

present a Letter of Administration before granting access to a deceased person’s bank account.
There are a few documents you will need when applying for a Letter of Administration. The exact

list may vary slightly from state to state -- but you will generally need the following documents:

· ***The original death certificate***
· ***A copy of the Will, if there was one***
· ***A statement of assets and liabilities within the Estate***
· ***A copy of the titles for any property owned (real estate, vehicles, etc.)***
· ***Letters from any banks where accounts are held***
· ***Certificates of valuations for any remaining assets***
*It takes anywhere from six to eight weeks to obtain the Letters of Administration -- assuming the application was filed with all of the necessary documents. There are a few factors that can extend this timeline, for example, if there is a disagreement over who to name as the Administrator of Estate. Because the processing time can vary it is generally recommended that you file an application for the Letters of Administration as soon as possible after the death of a loved one.*

Ø **Receive grant of probate or letters of administration from the court**

- A ***Grant of Probate*** is an order of the Court to confirm that the Executors named in a Will are the correct people to deal with the estate of someone who has died. The Grant of Probate gives the Executors the legal right to deal with the assets including property, bank accounts, shares, etc.

**YES**
Ø **Find the *executors* of the will**
- *The executor and guardians for children are usually named in your will; the health care proxy, living will, and durable power of attorney are usually distinct legal documents authorizing specific individuals to carry out certain tasks.*

Ø **Prepare your application for probate **

- This includes things like ***property***, ***debts***, ***bank accounts***, ***pensions,*** and other ***financial assets***.

Ø **Receive grant of probate or letters of administration from the court**
- A ***Grant of Probate*** is an order of the Court to confirm that the Executors named in a Will are the correct people to deal with the estate of someone who has died. The Grant of Probate gives the Executors the legal right to deal with the assets including property, bank accounts, shares, etc.

Ø **Inform any beneficiaries of their entitlements and responsibilities**
- The next step in the process is to list out and notify relatives. While you may have already spoken to family members about the deceased, you will need to alert potential heirs in an official capacity. *The purpose of this step is to inform anyone who might inherit a portion of the Estate or step in to serve as Administrator.*
- You may want to inform other organizations and accounts such as banks, memberships,
tax and insurance.
Ø **Collect any assets included in the estate, including vehicles, materials, and property**
Ø **Pay off any debts**
- The executor must pay debts and other financial obligations before distributing your assets. So, although your heirs or chosen beneficiaries are not personally responsible for paying your debts, the amount of money or property they receive may be affected by the amount of your debt.
Ø **Determine the final value of the estate**
Ø **Final distribution of estate between beneficiaries**

pages.title: How to fill-out LSH Daily Task Tracker
pages.summary: This provides an organized way of tracking daily tasks per client.
pages.body:
## What is this

This provides an organized way of tracking daily tasks per client.

## Why we do it this way

Legal Support Help needs a standard way of tracking daily tasks per client in order to monitor new, pending, ongoing, priority and completed tasks per client to ensure that tasks are accomplished on time and that will be able to extend help to VAs who are swamped with tasks.

## How we do this

Each VAs will be provided access to their client’s LSH Daily Task Tracker (if you still don’t have access, kindly coordinate with you POC)

### Sheet Name: LSH Daily Task Tracker | [Law Firm]

![](/img/53c84221b49180a7)

1. Fill-in the date when a task has been delegated or started on the “Date Received” column, once done
provide the “Actual Completion Date” in order for you to monitor your progress on how long you usually
complete a particular task given you need to manage multiple tasks and/or clients.

![](/img/8d3af10e29816660)

2. Provide what “Type of Task” you are about to do and fill-in the “Task Details / Specific Task” column, this may
be a copy paste instruction from your client’s message, all the information you need to accomplish a task
(such as client’s name, callback number, medical providers name etc.) or simply a brief summary of your task.

![](/img/172d8825dd43a1a1)
![](/img/9978ed3902a3945d)
![](/img/36eb0d7acc3f5791)

3. “Accountable VA” column is the name of the assigned Virtual Assistant accountable to accomplish the task.
Since we are using one (1) tracker for each client and there are instances where two (2) VAs are working for
the client we need to specify who is responsible for each task.

![](/img/1dc08e5f657bf4d8)

4. DAILY NOTES serves as your notepad for the recent or last updates on a work-in-progress task. Insert
another column for today’s date (don’t missed a date) in case you need to log any significant progress or
difficulties you’ve encountered, but you are not required to fill-in notes every single day, this will also serve
as your reference if needed for review on why a particular task has been accomplished longer than usual.
You can also use this as your calendar reminder for a future follow-up or task.

![](/img/122ccae94ffebfeb)

5. Tagged each task with either of the following statuses and updated as soon as the tasks became pending for
>3 days up to completed.

![](/img/20d545088c563791)
![](/img/ebdbe10c8879a123)

6. All tasks should be under **⬇ FOR COMPLETION⬇ **but if it's something you have to do on a regular basis
(weekly, monthly, quarterly, semi-annual, annual) such as (example: Follow-up Medical Providers (once a
week), Generate client invoice (monthly), Generate client statute of limitations report (monthly) Generate
full-year financial report (annual)) it should fall under **⬇ RECURRING⬇ **

*** IMPORTANT: Status of “recurring” tasks are always Ongoing or Priority-Ongoing unless you will no longer
need to do it on a regular basis that’s when you will move it under ⬇ COMPLETED ⬇. In addition, those under
“for completion”, once status is Completed you can now move the task below COMPLETED.***

![](/img/0b3d41f779b8882e)

7. “VA / POC NOTES” column is only used if there are additional or special instructions from POC such as
(example: Need to delegate to back-up VA, Long overdue need to prioritize, For turnover and the like)

![](/img/e866ce556d2c0739)

8. The highlighted portion will provide you a summary of your number of tasks according to statuses as of to
date. This will give you a quick overview if you are under task, on track or swamped which you can share to
your POC so they can extend help if needed.

![](/img/66ea0378f8002626)

9. The highlighted portion will provide you a summary of your **completed tasks as of the current month**. So
update the range of formulas for "Completed" every first day of the month.

***AGAIN, IMPORTANT: Status of “recurring” tasks are always Ongoing or Priority-Ongoing unless you will no
longer need to do it on a regular basis that’s when you will move it under ⬇ COMPLETED ⬇. In addition,
those under “for completion”, once status is Completed you can now move the task below COMPLETED.***

### Sheet Name: Client-VA Specific Tasks Index

This should provide general information on what are your specific tasks as VA of a particular law firm, this is a work-in-progress index since most of the time your tasks, duties and responsibilities expands depending on how well you are able to adjust to clients needs and demands. This also serves as our guide on what are the usual tasks delegated to you versus other VAs of the same or other areas of law which can open more tasks opportunities. We will also use this as reference for training of new VAs and/or upskill of existing VAs.

![](/img/da75f4ad90df2db9)

### Sheet Name: Links & Access

Log here tools and applications credentials, frequently visited links and used accesses. For security purposes, we are keeping all clients' credentials in our Lastpass account and by keeping this up-to-date we can regularly update those credentials. This also serves as our guide on what tools and applications you are using versus other VAs of the same or other areas of law which can open more upskill opportunities.

![](/img/162562adf684f6c2)

**Directory **-log here frequently contacted information in order to lessen your time spending on searching for previously dialed information.

![](/img/f3a2c23705ff5f3e)

**Time Zone - **be familiar that in the U.S. there are multiple time zones depending on your state assignment so you should know what time zone it is on your clients location and how to convert time.

*Example: You’ll have a meeting with your POC at 8AM (PST) following Nevada headquarters time zone, your client is following Eastern Standard Time (EST) and you are located in the Philippines. Therefore, 8AM (PST) = 11AM (EST) = 11PM (PH) are you available? *

This is important to ensure that there will be no schedule or tasks conflict from your end before you confirm any appointments. Same thing when you are handling appointment setting and calling clients from different states. We don’t want attorneys to miss an appointment because you forgot to consider their client’s time zone.

*Read more: Difference Between Standard Time and Daylight Time (*[*https://askanydifference.com/difference-between-standard-time-and-daylight-time/*](https://askanydifference.com/difference-between-standard-time-and-daylight-time/)*)*

![](/img/c73cbab339158a44)

pages.title: Receptionist Work Guide
pages.summary: This provides the Standard Operating Procedures in answering phone calls for Virtual Receptionists.
pages.body:
## What this is

This provides the Standard Operating Procedures in answering phone calls for Virtual Receptionists.

## Why we do it this way

Legal Support Help needs a standard way of handling calls anytime of the day and proper way of accommodating whoever calls in, call flow process, taking messages and documentation procedures, to ensure that Attorneys never lose a client because of rude receptionists who does not know how to handle a specific call type, and that we will never give out important information to any third-party callers.

## How we do this

![](/img/9bbc6825f65670d4)

# I. Things to remember before taking calls

**IMPORTANT: **It is recommended to set-up your tools 15 mins before your shift and log in / time-in 5 mins before your shift. This is to ensure that you will not encounter any issues since you are expected to take calls at the strike of the clock.

1. Before your official first day with the client, you should download their softphone’s computer desktop app.
2. Together with your POC / IT Support, using client’s softphone credentials you should conduct a test call on how to make an outbound call, answer an inbound call, placing on hold, cold transfer, warm transfer and conference call. NEVER place the caller on mute.
3. Make sure when you get a call it should have a ring ring sound and a notification should pop-up on the lower right portion of your screen.
4. As needed, request to Attorney their SOPs on relaying reception calls information, who to coordinate with, where to post or send updates. It is mandatory to track all received incoming calls as this serves as your documentation.
5. As needed, request to Attorney their phone number, fax number and email directories on where to transfer or refer a specific call to lessen the search time and increase your response time whenever you are on a call, remember that during day time there are times you might need to answer two (2) calls consecutively and assist more than one (1) call simultaneously, the following may or may not apply:
6. As needed, request to Attorney their phone number, fax number and email directories on where to transfer or refer a specific call to lessen the search time and increase your response time whenever you are on a call, remember that during day time there are times you might need to answer two (2) calls consecutively and assist more than one (1) call simultaneously, the following may or may not apply:
- E-mail access where the fax documents of clients and/or third-party will be received, in case you need to verify if a document has been received from your end.
- E-mail where you can send a request to fax a document to clients and/or third-party, in case you need to send a fax.
- Client issued email (e.g. jane@vanlawfirm.com) - in cases you need to send/receive direct emails.
- Directory of phone numbers and extensions of receptionists / intake specialist callers, your POC, Per Team (Case Managers (CM), Claims Assistants (CA), Senior and Junior callers), and Attorneys, if necessary.
- Schedule of receptionists / intake specialist callers, your POC, Per Team (Case Managers (CM), Claims Assistants (CA), Senior and Junior callers), and Attorneys, if necessary - so you know who to communicate with during your shift regarding a specific call if there are multiple shifts in the law firm.
- Common documents/forms the you need to send to clients and/or third-party - if applicable
- Attorneys Referral List - if applicable
- Doctors Referral List - if applicable

*Note on Directory:*

*a. We don’t transfer right away simply because a client or third-party is looking for a specific * *officer, the caller should pass verification questions and that the officer they are looking for * *should be someone who does accept calls in general or can accept calls at the moment.*

*b. There are also organizational movements (people will be assigned to new designations or already resigned) so make sure your Directory is always up-to-date.*

7. Always have your **Notepad **ready.This is where you will type-in everything so you won’t forget anything from the call. There are some receptionists who record their calls so they can listen again in case they are having difficulty understanding a specific caller's accent.
8. If needed, open a separate browser for email / mailroom in case you need it in sending and receiving direct messages / SMS.
9. A good reception call should have the following information (this may vary depending on Law Firm):

**Date & Time of call:**

**Caller’s name:**

**Callback number:**

**Client / Company?**

**If insurance, date of loss & claim#:**

**Summary of call:**

*Documentation: 11/15/21 10:25AM John Doe from State Farm CB#7025291122 for Ana Smith DOL 01/01/21 claim#123-ABC calling about treatment status *

**IMPORTANT**: Some Law Firms need to verify the caller using their CRM/CMS, whether the client is really represented by the firm. Confirm with the Attorney if they have specific security questions that the caller needs to pass before disclosing more information.

10. Confirm with the Attorney if you will also take new leads / potential client calls. If YES, then request for SOP Questions for all possible case scenarios that you may receive, so in case you received a New Lead = Potential Client calls you are ready to own it. For more information refer to Knowledge Base article:** Intake Specialist**
11. **Hubstaff Tracker, **Law FirmProjects, To-Do and Add Notes should be set-up, organized and utilized.

![](/img/d1f6012ef54b347a)

13.** Task Tracker **, it is mandatory to track all your calls and tasks as this serves as your supporting document in the future. For more information refer to Knowledge Base article:** How to fill-out LSH Daily Task Tracker**

![](/img/265a3a27e40e92e6)

# II. CALL TYPES

Call types may vary depending on your client’s Areas of Law, below are the common call types:

### 1. Client with existing records on CRM/CMS (e.g. Filevine)

a. Get the first and last name of the client (make sure the spelling is correct) and Date of Loss / Accident then Search for a project in CRM/CMS.

b. If nothing shows up, there are cases that the person is calling on behalf of the client on file (such as parents, child, sibling, partner), verify whose name is associated with the case.

c. If you found the records, don’t disclose any information, check the Case Type, Case Manager and Claims Assistant to know who to coordinate the call

### 2. Other Attorney / Court Representative / Litigation-Related

Unless it is another attorney (opposing counsel) most calls should be handled by the attorney’s assigned paralegal (CMs, CAs, Sr. and Jr. callers).

This means if it is a client, pharmacy, or medical facility calling it should go to the paralegal.

The attorneys are terribly busy handling more important matters so the paralegals take majority of the calls.

They will reach out to the attorneys if they need to.

### 3. Insurance Companies

Aside from the information you will ask at the onset of the call, ALWAYS ASK for a CLAIM NUMBER when receiving a call from Insurance Companies.

Insurance companies will always ask for index information of clients (such as DOB, SSN which can be used against the client and law firm). WE DO NOT GIVE THAT INFORMATION EVER!

Confirm with the Attorney what information you are allowed to disclose or where to direct this kind of calls.

If they give you a hard time on the phone you can let them know it’s the company policy.

And that any requests should be send in written via Fax or Mail.

### 4. Medical Provider Request (e.g. Meds Approval)

Confirm with the Attorney what information you are allowed to disclose or where to direct this kind of calls.

For example, when a pharmacy calls for a medicine approval in case the right person are not available take a message and get the following information:

**[SOP Questions for Med Approvals]**

Who is calling and from where:

The prescribing Doctor for the Rx:

The Rx total:

The total on the account after the Rx:

*Documentation: Michelle w/Partell regarding meds approval, RX price $41.75, New * *Balance $120, Dr Steven Olenchak, would like a call bak P: 702-91-380*

### 5. Client Request (e.g. Uber)

Confirm with the Attorney what information you are allowed to disclose or where to direct this kind of calls.

### 6. Inquiry on cases that Attorney handles

To learn more about the cases Attorney handles, review their company website.

### 7. New Leads = Potential Clients

For more information refer to Knowledge Base article:** Intake Specialist**

# III. CALL FLOW

### 1. Response Time Protocol:

**Golden Rule: **Answer on the first ring **(One Ring Policy).**

- *If this is a New Lead/Potential Client, on the second ring* *we might lose it, which means expenses = waste of money.*
- *If this is an Existing Client / for an Existing Client, on the second ring we might lose important information, yes we can call back and chase them but we could have just saved time.*

### 2. Opening Spiel:

Ask Attorney if they have a standard opening spiel, if none you may use:

**“IT'S A GREAT DAY AT _____ LAW FIRM! THIS IS [YOUR NAME], HOW MAY I HELP YOU?”**

### 3. Get the necessary information

***(this may vary depending on Law Firm)***

**Date & Time of call:**

**Caller’s name:**

**Callback number:**

**Client / Company?**

**If insurance, date of loss & claim#:**

**Summary of call:**

### 4. During the call they may provide a name of the person they wanted to speak with.

You may also verify in case they haven’t mentioned one:

*“Is there anyone you would like to speak with? Let me see if they are available.”*

### 5. Hold Protocol

5.a.) Before you place the call on hold, let the caller know that you are about to place them on hold and approximately for how long. This is to show courtesy and set proper expectations.

*“May I place you on hold for a minute or two so I can check if they are available?”*

*“May I place you on hold for 2-3 minutes so I can check if they are available?”*

5.b.) Do not place a call on hold for more than 3 minutes, if you need more time you should go back to the caller and let them know that you still need to place them on hold for another minute or so. This is to avoid making them upset for waiting and worst hang-up! Callers wanted update or at least know what was going on.

### 6. Handling Time Protocol

6.a.) You are expected to handle a regular call (such as general inquiry, transfer) in less than 3-5 minutes for PRO up to maximum of 6-8 minutes for beginners.

6.b.) Except for Call Type – New Leads = Potential Clients which may take more time, follow applicable handling protocols. NEVER rush this type of call.

### 7. Call On Queue / Call Waiting Protocol

Especially on peak hours you will be receiving volume of calls and there are instances that you will need to accommodate more than one (1) call simultaneously.

**7.a.) **Since you are obviously still with another call, advice your first call that you will need to place them on a brief hold:

*“[Name of First Caller] May I place you on a brief hold?” - this is the recommended spiel as you don't want to tell the first caller you are going to accommodate another call while you are not yet done assisting them.*

**7.b.) **Once you answered the second call, immediately let them know that you will need to place them on a brief hold:

*“ It’s a Great Day at _____ Law Firm! This is [Your Name] speaking. May I place you on a brief hold?”*

**7.c.)** If they respond or not before you place the second caller on hold just say:

*“Thank you. Stay on the line please.”*

**7.d.) ** Then go back to your first caller and proceed with the call flow.

**7.e.) ** Don’t forget that you still have the second or third call, as applicable proceed with the call flow.

**REMINDER**: You should only accommodate more than two (2) calls simultaneously if it will not affect your service level.

**IMPORTANT: Service Level **is achieved if you are able to:

**#1. Answer the Call on the First Ring and **

**#2. Accommodate the call in less than 3-5 minutes. **

### 8. Handling irate clients

- Stay calm and courteous
- Let customers vent and actively listen, take notes as needed
- Use the right tone of voice
- Don’t react - less talk, less mistake
- Acknowledge their feelings but be neutral
- Advice that their concern will be forwarded to the case manager / attorney and that someone will call back within 24 business hours or as soon as the right person is available (this may vary depending on Law Firm)
- Don’t over promise
- Don’t take it personally - they are shouting out of frustration, it's not about you

# IV. TRANSFERRING A CALL

There are two (2) types of call transfer:

### a.) Cold Transfer

– is when you transfer the call right away without advising your caller they are about to be transferred to another line. This is not recommended as it may result to drop call / call disconnected, so before you place your caller on hold advise them that in case the person is available or anyone is available to assist you will immediately put them through the line – setting proper expectations.

### b.) Warm Transfer

– is when you introduce both parties to one another or at least make sure (by listening) that the call was transferred properly neither dropped nor disconnected. This is recommended especially when volumes of calls are low – showing courtesy

*Note: If there is misleading or conflicting information, updated procedures and new protocols kindly leave a comment / suggest an update below so we can incorporate / update immediately. *

*Gwen Paiso – November 15, 2021*
